definition_zh: 绩效评估；性能评测；表现评价
definition_en: a formal judgement of how well a person, a machine or an activity has done against agreed standards
core_image: 年终考评的会议室里，主管在评分表上逐项打分，旁边的投影显示着全年产出曲线
scene: 年终考评会上，主管对照评分表逐项记下每个人这一年的产出与协作情况。 The annual performance evaluation compares each worker's output with agreed targets.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「对照既定目标判断工作成效的正式评估」（第 1 个义项：对员工年度工作成果的正式评定）；句意为年度绩效评估把每位员工的产出与商定目标作比较。图中可辨识物件：评分表、产出曲线、会议桌、签字笔。

pos.zh: 绩效评估（可数名词短语）
性能评测；表现评价（可数名词短语）

derivatives.zh: 表现不佳；业绩低于预期

senses.title: A formal judgement of a worker's year
senses.definition: the periodic review in which a manager rates an employee's results against set goals
senses.definitionCN: 主管对照既定目标，定期评定员工业绩的程序
senses.example: The annual performance evaluation compares each worker's output with agreed targets.
senses.exampleCN: 年度绩效评估把每位员工的产出与商定目标作比较。
senses.why: Performance here means how well someone carried out the job, and evaluation means fixing its worth, so the phrase is a judgement of work done.
senses.whyCN: 这里的前一个词指工作执行得如何，后一个词指判定其价值，因此这个短语就是对已完成工作的评判。

senses.title: A test of how well a machine works
senses.definition: a measured assessment of the speed, accuracy or efficiency of a device under stated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在规定条件下对装置速度、精度或效率的测量评定
senses.example: A performance evaluation of the new pump showed a ten percent gain.
senses.exampleCN: 对新泵的性能评测显示效率提高了百分之十。
senses.why: Machines also perform, so the same phrase moved from people to equipment and now means a bench test.
senses.whyCN: 机器也在「表现」，因此同一短语从人转到设备，如今指台架测试。

senses.title: A review of whether a project met its aims
senses.definition: an assessment of a programme's delivery against its plan, often required by funders
senses.definitionCN: 对照计划评定某项目的交付情况，常由出资方要求
senses.example: The donors asked for a performance evaluation halfway through the project.
senses.exampleCN: 出资方要求在项目进行到一半时做一次执行评估。
senses.why: A project performs in the sense of delivering, so its mid-course review took the same name as a staff appraisal.
senses.whyCN: 项目在「交付」意义上也在表现，因此其中期评审与员工考核用了同一名称。

senses.title: An assessment of a student's demonstrated work
senses.definition: a judgement based on what a learner actually produces rather than on a single test score
senses.definitionCN: 依据学习者实际完成的成果而非单次考试分数作出的评定
senses.example: Teachers use a performance evaluation rubric rather than a single test score.
senses.exampleCN: 教师用表现评价量表，而不是只看一次考试分数。
senses.why: Education borrowed the phrase to separate what a student does from what a test measures, and a rubric makes the judgement explicit.
senses.whyCN: 教育借这个短语把学生实际做到的事与考试测到的东西分开，评分量表使这种判断明确可见。

senses.title: A review of an organization's results
senses.titleCN: 组织或子公司业绩评估
senses.definition: a formal judgement of how a division or subsidiary has performed over a period
senses.definitionCN: 对某部门或子公司在某一时期业绩的正式评定
senses.example: The board's performance evaluation of the subsidiary led to a sale.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会对该子公司的业绩评估最终导致将其出售。
senses.why: Whole units are judged by results too, so the phrase scales from one worker to an entire company.
senses.whyCN: 整个单位也按结果受评，因此这个短语可以从一名员工扩展到一整家公司。

senses.title: A benchmark of a model or algorithm
senses.definition: a measured comparison of a system's accuracy, speed or cost on a fixed set of tasks
senses.definitionCN: 在固定任务集上对系统准确率、速度或成本的测量比较
senses.example: The team ran a performance evaluation of three speech models on the same data.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在同一批数据上对三个语音模型做了性能评估。
senses.why: Software performs on tasks, so testing it against a fixed set became another performance evaluation.
senses.whyCN: 软件在任务上「表现」，因此在固定任务集上测试它，又成了一种性能评估。

senses.title: The measurement of actual language use
senses.definition: in linguistics, the study of real utterances rather than of the underlying knowledge that produces them
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中研究实际说出的话语，而非产生话语的底层知识
senses.example: A performance evaluation in linguistics looks at actual utterances rather than idealized knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学中的运用评估考察实际说出的话语，而非理想化的知识。
senses.why: The field separates competence from performance, and measuring the latter is literally evaluating how language is performed.
senses.whyCN: 该学科把语言能力与语言运用分开，测量后者字面上就是评估语言被运用的情形。

senses.title: A judgement of athletic execution
senses.definition: a technical review of how a movement was executed, often from video
senses.definitionCN: 对某一动作完成质量的技术性评审，常借助录像
senses.example: Coaches video each sprint for a performance evaluation of technique.
senses.exampleCN: 教练为每次冲刺录像，用来做技术表现评估。
senses.why: Sport performs before an audience, so the review of technique inherited the word from the stage as much as from the office.
senses.whyCN: 运动在观众面前「表现」，因此对技术的评审既承自办公室，也承自舞台。

intro.en: The phrase joins a verb of carrying something through to a noun of worth. Performance came through Old French from a verb meaning to complete; evaluation came from French and rests on a Latin verb meaning to be worth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个表示「把事做完」的动词与一个表示「价值」的名词连在一起。前者经古法语出自意为「完成」的动词；后者来自法语，底子是拉丁语中表示「有价值」的动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Par- 'thoroughly' plus fournir 'to provide' produced parfournir 'to carry out to the end, to complete'. The origin of fournir is uncertain, possibly Germanic.
items.cn: par-「彻底」加 fournir「提供」构成 parfournir，意为「做到最后、完成」。fournir 的来源不确定，可能出自日耳曼语。

items.en: Valere meant 'to be strong, to be well, to be worth'. Its deeper origin is a reconstruction, so source uncertain below Latin.
items.cn: valere 意为「强壮、健康、有价值」。其更深来源属重构形式，故拉丁语以下来源不确定。

items.en: French évaluer 'to fix the value of' was formed on value, and English evaluation entered in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 法语中表示「确定价值」的动词由「价值」构成，这个词于十九世纪进入英语。

items.en: Performance first meant the carrying out of a task or the giving of a play, and only later the measured efficiency of a machine.
items.cn: 这个词最初指任务的完成或戏剧的演出，后来才指机器的实测效率。

items.en: Personnel management joined the two words in the twentieth century, and the phrase spread to equipment, projects and models.
items.cn: 二十世纪人事管理把这两个词连在一起，此后该短语扩及设备、项目与模型。

note.en: Group one holds phrases that share one of the two words but judge a different thing; group two holds single words for judging worth or performance.
note.cn: 第一组是共用其中一个词、但评判对象不同的短语；第二组是表示评判价值或表现的单字词。

entries.definition: The human-resources term for the same staff review; appraisal stresses the interview and the rating form.
entries.definitionCN: 人力资源领域对同一种员工考核的叫法，更强调面谈与评分表。

entries.definition: A periodic look back at results; it may be informal and need not produce a score.
entries.definitionCN: 定期回顾成果，可以是非正式的，未必给出分数。

entries.definition: The continuing system of goals, feedback and rewards, of which one evaluation is a step.
entries.definitionCN: 目标、反馈与奖励的持续体系，单次评估只是其中一步。

entries.definition: A measure that signals how well something is going; it feeds an evaluation but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 指示运行状况的指标，供评估使用，但本身不是评估。

entries.definition: A judgement of the level or quality reached, often broader than one person's yearly results.
entries.definitionCN: 对达到的水平或质量所作判断，范围常比一名员工的年度成果更宽。

entries.definition: A judgement of value, used for property, staff and projects alike.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值的判定，可用于房产、员工与项目。

entries.definition: A formal check of accounts or compliance against rules, not of how well work was done.
entries.definitionCN: 对账目或合规情况的正式核查，而非评断工作做得好不好。

entries.definition: A standard against which results are compared; it supplies the yardstick rather than the verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 用来比较结果的标准，提供尺子而不给出结论。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first word names how a task was carried out; the second names the act of fixing its worth.
normal.cn: 前一个词指任务执行得如何，后一个词指判定其价值的动作。

normal.en: One family runs perform, performance, performer and underperform; the other runs value, evaluate, evaluation and evaluator.
normal.cn: 一族是同出「执行」的词，另一族是同出「价值」的词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the setting: annual performance evaluation, evaluation criteria, evaluation report.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：年度绩效评估、评估标准、评估报告。

normal.en: The phrase moves from staff to pumps, projects, students, models and sprinters, because all of them perform.
normal.cn: 这个短语从员工转到泵、项目、学生、模型与短跑者，因为它们都在「表现」。

normal.en: An indicator is a number; an evaluation is a judgement made with that number.
normal.cn: 指标是一个数字；评估是用这个数字作出的判断。

abstract.en: Picture a form with boxes, and a pen that hesitates before the last one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张带格子的表格，笔在最后一格前停了一停。

abstract.en: Picture two runners and one stopwatch shared between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者和一只两人共用的秒表。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror that reports not what you look like but how far you have come.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子，照出的不是你的样子，而是你走了多远。

examples.en: The union objected that the performance evaluation rewarded speed over safety.
examples.cn: 工会反对说，绩效评估奖励速度而轻视安全。

examples.en: A performance evaluation of the battery pack is due before winter.
examples.cn: 电池组的性能评测要在入冬前完成。

examples.en: Without a performance evaluation, the grant cannot be renewed.
examples.cn: 没有执行评估，这笔资助就无法续期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「performance（表现）+ evaluation（评估）」——看表现再打分 → 绩效评估、性能评测

root: 这个短语的前半经古法语出自意为「做到最后」的动词，由「彻底」前缀加「提供」动词构成，后者来源不确定；后半经法语出自「价值」，再上溯拉丁语表示「有价值、强壮」的动词，其更早词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of judging: a worker's year is rated, a machine is bench-tested, a project is reviewed, a student's work is scored, a subsidiary is judged, a model is benchmarked, actual language use is measured, and a movement is filmed and graded.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个评判动作展开：评员工一年、试机器性能、审项目交付、给学生成果打分、判子公司业绩、给模型做基准、测实际语言运用，最后给一个动作录像评分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ratings sheet on a meeting table, every row compared with a target written in the same column.
core.cn: 核心意象：会议桌上的一张评分表，每一行都与同一列写着的目标对照。

branches.en: JUDGING PEOPLE: a worker's year and a student's work are rated by what was actually produced.
branches.cn: 评判人：员工的一年与学生的成果，都按实际产出评定。

branches.en: JUDGING EXECUTION: a pump on a bench and a sprint on video are both measured for how well they ran.
branches.cn: 评判执行：台架上的泵与录像里的冲刺，都在测它们运行得多好。

branches.en: JUDGING A WHOLE EFFORT: a project and a subsidiary are assessed against a plan and a target.
branches.cn: 评判整体：项目与子公司都对照计划与目标受评。

branches.en: JUDGING A MODEL: a fixed task set turns performance into a number to compare.
branches.cn: 评判模型：固定任务集把表现变成一个可比较的数字。

branches.en: JUDGING USE: linguistics measures utterances rather than the knowledge behind them.
branches.cn: 评判运用：语言学测量说出的话语，而非话语背后的知识。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two histories: a French verb of completing a task and a Latin-rooted noun of worth, each with its own family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两段历史构成：一个法语来源、表示「完成任务」的动词，以及一个拉丁词根、表示「价值」的名词，各自带一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere gives value, evaluate, evaluation and valuable; the French verb behind perform gives performance and performer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「有价值」的动词衍生出价值与评估等词；表示「完成」的法语动词则衍生出表现与表演者。

items.example: The source verb is French, and its own origin is uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 这个源动词出自法语，其本身来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks doing a thing to the end.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记把事做到最后。

items.meaning: to carry through to the end
items.example: Completion is the core of the first half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 「完成」是这个短语前半的核心。

items.meaning: to carry out, to do, to act
items.example: A task and a stage role are both carried out.
items.exampleCN: 任务与舞台角色都要被「做出来」。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the name of its doing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把动词变成其「做」的名称。

items.meaning: to be strong, to be worth
items.example: Worth is strength in the older sense of the word.
items.exampleCN: 价值在较早的词义里就是力量。

items.example: The noun names what something is worth.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指某物值多少。

items.example: To evaluate is to put a figure on worth.
items.exampleCN: 评估就是给价值定一个数。

items.example: The suffix makes the judging a named process.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把评判变成一个有名称的过程。

items.example: The agent suffix names the judge.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指作出评判的人。

latinEntries.meaning: to be strong, to be worth

definition_zh: 驱散；消除（疑虑、恐惧、误解）
definition_en: to drive something away and make it disappear, especially a feeling or a false idea
core_image: 清晨的雾压在湖面上，一阵风从岸边推过来，把整片白气撕开、赶走
scene: 会议开始前，走廊里的人越聚越多，他拿出一份数据。 A single chart dispelled the rumour within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 dispel 指把谣言赶走（第 3 个义项：驳斥谣言）；句意为一张图表几分钟内就驱散了谣言。

pos.zh: 驱散；消除；驳斥

senses.title: Drive away a fear
senses.definition: to make a fear lose its hold on a person
senses.definitionCN: 使恐惧失去对人的控制
senses.example: Her calm voice dispelled the child's fear of the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静的声音驱散了孩子对黑暗的恐惧。
senses.why: Fear behaves like mist: it blurs everything until something warm moves through it.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧像雾：它把一切弄模糊，直到有温暖的东西穿过去。

senses.title: Scatter a crowd
senses.definition: to make a gathered group break up and leave
senses.definitionCN: 使聚集的人群散开离去
senses.example: The guards dispelled the crowd before the gates opened.
senses.exampleCN: 大门开启前，守卫驱散了人群。
senses.why: A crowd is held together by a shared mood; once that mood breaks, the bodies follow.
senses.whyCN: 人群由共同的情绪聚在一起；情绪一散，身体也就跟着散了。

senses.title: Refute a rumour
senses.definition: to show that a story is false so that people stop believing it
senses.definitionCN: 证明传言不实，使人不再相信
senses.example: A single chart dispelled the rumour within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 一张图表几分钟内就驱散了谣言。
senses.why: A rumour lives on belief alone, so evidence is the wind that clears it.
senses.whyCN: 谣言只靠相信存活，因此证据就是吹散它的那阵风。

senses.title: Break an illusion
senses.definition: to destroy a false picture that someone has been holding
senses.definitionCN: 摧毁某人一直抱持的错误图景
senses.example: The first rehearsal dispelled any illusion of ease.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次排练就打碎了任何轻松的幻想。
senses.why: An illusion is a picture kept in place by hope; contact with the real thing removes it.
senses.whyCN: 幻想是被希望撑住的图景；与真实接触就会把它移走。

senses.title: Clear mist or fog
senses.definition: to make mist, fog or smoke thin out and vanish
senses.definitionCN: 使雾、烟变薄并消失
senses.example: A warm wind dispelled the fog over the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵暖风吹散了港口上的雾。
senses.why: This is the word's oldest picture: something visible but without substance is moved away.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的画面：可见却无实质的东西被移开。

senses.title: Remove a doubt
senses.definition: to settle a question in someone's mind so that doubt ends
senses.definitionCN: 在某人心中解决一个问题，使疑虑终止
senses.example: One sentence from the doctor dispelled her doubts.
senses.exampleCN: 医生的一句话消除了她的疑虑。
senses.why: Doubt is a fog in the mind, and a clear answer works like wind on it.
senses.whyCN: 疑虑是心里的雾，一个清楚的回答就像吹在雾上的风。

senses.title: Banish a mood
senses.definition: to make a heavy or gloomy mood lift from a place or group
senses.definitionCN: 使沉重或阴郁的气氛从某处或某群人中散开
senses.example: His joke dispelled the gloom of the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑话驱走了会议的阴郁。
senses.why: Moods hang in a room like smoke; a single bright act can clear the air.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像烟一样悬在房间里；一个明亮的举动就能让空气清朗。

senses.title: Dispel darkness
senses.definition: to drive back darkness with light, literally or as an image
senses.definitionCN: 用光逼退黑暗，无论实指或比喻
senses.example: The first lamp dispelled the darkness of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 第一盏灯驱散了门厅的黑暗。
senses.why: Darkness is the clearest case of something that retreats when something else arrives.
senses.whyCN: 黑暗是「别的东西一来就退走」最清楚的例子。

intro.en: Dispel is built from a prefix meaning apart and a verb meaning to drive, so it says exactly what it does: drive apart.
intro.cn: dispel 由一个意为「分开」的前缀和一个意为「驱赶」的动词构成，因此它说的就是它做的：赶开。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 17c. from Latin, first used of clouds and then of fears.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪从拉丁语借入这个动词，最初用于云，后来用于恐惧。

items.en: Dispellere meant 'to drive apart, to scatter', used of troops and of weather.
items.cn: dispellere 意为「赶开、驱散」，用于军队，也用于天气。

items.en: The prefix dis- means apart, in different directions, which gives the scattering motion.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 意为分开、朝不同方向，赋予它四散的动作。

items.en: Pellere 'to push, to drive' is also the root of compel and repel.
items.cn: pellere「推、驱」也是 compel 与 repel 的词根。

items.en: The verb moved from weather to the mind: rumours, doubts and fears are now what get dispelled.
items.cn: 这个动词从天气移到心智：如今被驱散的是谣言、疑虑与恐惧。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the pell drive; the near-meaning group names other ways of making something disappear.
note.cn: 形近组保留 pell「推、驱」；近义组列出其它让事物消失的方式。

entries.definition: able to be driven away.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被驱散的。

entries.definition: in the act of driving something away.
entries.definitionCN: 正在把某物驱散。

entries.definition: to push something back from a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从表面推开。

entries.definition: to drive someone to act by force.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使某人行动。

entries.definition: to throw or drive things in different directions.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西朝不同方向抛开。

entries.definition: to make fear or worry less intense.
entries.definitionCN: 使恐惧或担忧减弱。

entries.definition: to prove that a claim is wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某个说法是错的。

entries.definition: to send something away so that it does not return.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物赶走使其不再回来。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of wind tearing a sheet of mist into pieces that drift away.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「风把一片雾撕成碎块、吹向远处」的画面。

normal.en: Dispel shares pell with repel: one pushes back, the other pushes apart.
normal.cn: dispel 与 repel 共享 pell：一个往后推，一个往四周推。

normal.en: Think of a fan switched on in a foggy room: the fog leaves, the fan stays.
normal.cn: 想象雾屋里打开一台风扇：雾走了，风扇还在。

normal.en: Spell it dis + pel; the single l is doubled only in the past: dispelled.
normal.cn: 拼作 dis + pel；只有过去式才双写 l：dispelled。

normal.en: Say dis-PEL; the stress lands on the push, not on the apart.
normal.cn: 读成 dis-PEL，重音落在「推」上，而不在「分开」上。

normal.en: A rumour is fog with a voice; evidence is the wind.
normal.cn: 谣言是有声音的雾；证据就是风。

abstract.en: What has no substance is easiest to drive away, which is why doubt yields to clarity.
abstract.cn: 没有实质的东西最容易被赶走，所以疑虑会向清晰让步。

abstract.en: Dispelling is not arguing; it is changing the air until the thing cannot stay.
abstract.cn: 驱散不是争论；它是改变空气，直到那东西待不下去。

abstract.en: A light does not fight darkness; it simply arrives.
abstract.cn: 光不与黑暗搏斗；它只是到达。

examples.en: A single chart dispelled the rumour within minutes.
examples.cn: 一张图表几分钟内就驱散了谣言。

examples.en: Her calm voice dispelled the child's fear of the dark.
examples.cn: 她平静的声音驱散了孩子对黑暗的恐惧。

examples.en: A warm wind dispelled the fog over the harbour.
examples.cn: 一阵暖风吹散了港口上的雾。

dict_mnemonic.text: dis（分开）+ pel（推）：把东西往四周推开，就是「驱散」。

root: 拉丁语 pellere（推、驱），加前缀 dis-（分开）→ dispellere

sensesIntro.en: Dispel always needs two things: something without solidity and a force that moves through it; the senses differ only in what the mist stands for.
sensesIntro.cn: dispel 总需要两样东西：一样没有实质的东西，以及一股穿过它的力量；各义项的差别只在雾代表什么。

core.en: DRIVING THE MIST AWAY
core.cn: 把雾赶走

branches.en: Literal mist and darkness moved away by wind or light.
branches.cn: 被风或光移走的真实的雾与黑暗。

branches.en: Inner weather: fear, doubt and gloom.
branches.cn: 内心的天气：恐惧、疑虑与阴郁。

branches.en: False stories and false pictures destroyed by evidence.
branches.cn: 被证据摧毁的假故事与假图景。

branches.en: A crowd losing the mood that held it together.
branches.cn: 人群失去维系它的那种情绪。

branches.en: The word moves easily from weather to the mind.
branches.cn: 这个词从天气轻松移到心智。

intro.en: The pell family is all about driving: repel pushes back, compel drives forward, expel drives out, dispel drives apart.
intro.cn: pell 词族全与「驱」有关：repel 往后推，compel 往前驱，expel 往外赶，dispel 往四周赶。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere gives the push; the prefix dis- decides the direction, and direction is the whole difference in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 提供推力，前缀 dis- 决定方向，而方向正是这个词族全部的区别。

items.meaning: to drive apart in all directions
to drive back toward its source
to drive out of a place

definition_zh: 生物钟；生物体内在计时系统；（通俗）生育时钟
definition_en: the internal timing system that coordinates daily and seasonal biological rhythms
core_image: 一枚嵌在身体深处的旧怀表，没人上弦，它自己走，还每天按窗外的光对一次时
scene: 换班工人的作息一周一变，身体却仍按旧时间表醒来。 A shift worker's biological clock rarely adjusts to a changing roster.
sceneCN: 这里 biological clock 指「体内自行计时的节律系统」（第 1 个义项：生物体内在计时机制）；句意为换班工人的生物钟很难适应不断变动的排班。图中可辨识物件：轮班表、遮光帘、床头闹钟、窗外天色。

pos.zh: 生物钟；生物体内在计时系统（可数，复数 biological clocks）
（通俗）生育时钟；生育年龄的时限感

collocations.zh: 生育时钟在走（年龄压力）

derivatives.zh: bios（希腊「生命」）+ -logia（学问）→ 研究生命的学科
biology + -ical（形容词后缀）→ 生物学的；生物的
中世纪拉丁 clocca「钟」→ 计时器；动词义为记录时间
clock + work → 钟表机构；像钟表一样规律运转的东西
bio-（生命）+ chronometry（测时）→ 生物计时测量

senses.title: The body's internal timekeeper
senses.definition: the set of internal mechanisms by which an organism times daily and seasonal changes
senses.definitionCN: 生物用来计时昼夜与季节变化的一整套内部机制
senses.example: A shift worker's biological clock rarely adjusts to a changing roster.
senses.exampleCN: 换班工人的生物钟很难适应不断变动的排班。
senses.why: The phrase joins a living body to a machine that keeps time: biology supplies the body, clock supplies the regular beat.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把活的躯体与计时的机械连在一起：biology 提供身体，clock 提供规律的节拍。

senses.title: The circadian pacemaker tissue
senses.definition: the specific group of cells, such as the suprachiasmatic nucleus, that generates the daily rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 产生日节律的特定细胞群，如视交叉上核
senses.example: The biological clock sits in a tiny cluster of cells above the optic chiasm.
senses.exampleCN: 生物钟位于视交叉上方一小簇细胞里。
senses.why: Once the general system was located, the phrase could name the tissue itself rather than the whole capacity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这套总体系统被定位，这个短语就能指组织本身，而非整体能力。

senses.title: The fertility deadline in everyday speech
senses.titleCN: 日常口语中的生育年龄时限
senses.definition: the informal sense of the age-related limit on a person's ability to have children
senses.definitionCN: 通俗义：与年龄相关的生育能力时限
senses.example: She felt her biological clock ticking and changed her plans.
senses.exampleCN: 她感觉自己的生育时钟在走，于是改变了计划。
senses.why: The metaphor treats reproductive capacity as a clock running down, which is why the phrase sounds urgent rather than scientific.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把生育能力当作一只走慢的钟，因此这个短语听起来紧迫而非科学。

senses.title: The gene and protein loop behind it
senses.titleCN: 支撑生物钟的基因与蛋白质回路
senses.definition: the molecular feedback circuit that produces a roughly daily cycle inside cells
senses.definitionCN: 在细胞内产生约日循环的分子反馈回路
senses.example: Researchers mapped the biological clock gene network in fruit flies.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员在果蝇中绘制了生物钟基因网络。
senses.why: A clock needs an oscillator, and the gene loop is the oscillator that keeps the hands moving.
senses.whyCN: 钟需要一个振荡器，而基因回路就是让指针继续走的振荡器。

senses.title: Synchronisation with the environment
senses.titleCN: 与环境授时因子的同步
senses.definition: the process by which light, temperature or social cues reset the internal clock each day
senses.definitionCN: 光、温度或社会线索每天重置内部钟的过程
senses.example: Morning light resets the biological clock after a late night.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨的光在熬夜之后重置生物钟。
senses.why: An internal clock drifts, so it needs a daily hand-setting from the outside world.
senses.whyCN: 内部钟会漂移，因此需要外部世界每天替它对一次表。

senses.title: Clock disruption and health risk
senses.titleCN: 生物钟紊乱与健康风险
senses.definition: the state in which the internal clock is out of step with sleep, work or daylight, with effects on health
senses.definitionCN: 内部钟与睡眠、工作或日光脱节、并影响健康的状态
senses.example: Long-term biological clock disruption is linked to metabolic problems.
senses.exampleCN: 长期的生物钟紊乱与代谢问题相关。
senses.why: When the clock and the schedule disagree, every daily process fires at the wrong hour.
senses.whyCN: 当钟与日程不一致时，每一项日常过程都在错误的时刻启动。

senses.title: The sense of time running out
senses.definition: a figurative use for the pressure of a deadline, especially an age-related one
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指截止期限带来的压力，尤指与年龄相关的期限
senses.example: The biological clock of the whole project was ticking loudly.
senses.exampleCN: 整个项目的生物钟在滴答作响。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the body only to express urgency: something living cannot wait forever.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借身体只为表达紧迫：活的东西不能无限期等待。

senses.title: The seasonal timer for migration or breeding
senses.titleCN: 安排迁徙或繁殖的季节计时器
senses.definition: the internal calendar that tells an organism when a season is approaching
senses.definitionCN: 告诉生物某一季节正在临近的内部日历
senses.example: A biological clock tells the bird when to fatten for migration.
senses.exampleCN: 生物钟告诉这只鸟何时为迁徙囤积脂肪。
senses.why: Daily clocks can also be read across the year, so the phrase covers seasonal timing as well as nightly timing.
senses.whyCN: 日钟也能跨年读取，因此这个短语既涵盖夜间计时，也涵盖季节计时。

intro.en: Biological clock joins biology, coined from Greek bios 'life' and -logia 'study', to clock, which comes through Middle Dutch and Medieval Latin clocca 'bell'. The phrase itself is a modern English combination whose first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: biological clock 把 biology（由希腊 bios「生命」与 -logia「学问」构成）与 clock（经中古荷兰语与中世纪拉丁 clocca「钟」而来）组合起来。这个短语本身是近代英语组合，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Bios meant 'life'. It supplies the bio- element in biology, biography and biodiversity.
items.cn: bios 意为「生命」，提供 biology、biography、biodiversity 中的 bio- 成分。

items.en: -Logia meant 'the study of', from logos 'word, reason'. Modern Latin turned bios and -logia into biologia in the early nineteenth century.
items.cn: -logia 意为「……的学问」，来自 logos「言词、理性」。近代拉丁在十九世纪初把 bios 与 -logia 合为 biologia。

items.en: Clocca meant 'bell' in Medieval Latin, probably borrowed from a Celtic word. It passed through Middle Dutch into English as clock, first for a bell struck to mark hours.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 clocca 意为「钟」，可能借自凯尔特语。它经中古荷兰语进入英语作 clock，最初指报时的钟铃。

items.en: When clocks became machines rather than bells, clock came to mean the instrument itself, and later any regular timer.
items.cn: 当钟从钟铃变成机械装置后，clock 开始指仪器本身，后来指任何规律计时器。

items.en: The phrase biological clock appears in twentieth-century physiology and then in popular writing about fertility. The exact first use is not firmly dated.
items.cn: biological clock 这一短语出现于二十世纪生理学，随后进入关于生育的通俗写作。确切最早用例没有可靠年代。

items.en: The fertility sense spread in the later twentieth century and gave the phrase its familiar urgency outside science.
items.cn: 生育义在二十世纪后期传开，使这个短语在科学之外获得人们熟悉的紧迫感。

note.en: Group one holds closely related clock phrases that differ in scope; group two holds other names for the body's timing system.
note.cn: 第一组是范围不同、关系极近的「钟」短语；第二组是身体计时系统的其他名称。

entries.definition: The everyday equivalent of biological clock in its rhythm sense; it never carries the fertility meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 在节律义上与 biological clock 对应的日常说法；从不带生育义。

entries.definition: The technical name for the roughly daily oscillator; it excludes seasonal timers that biological clock can cover.
entries.definitionCN: 约日振荡器的技术名称；不包含 biological clock 可涵盖的季节计时器。

entries.definition: The observable cycle itself rather than the mechanism that generates it.
entries.definitionCN: 可观察到的循环本身，而非产生它的机制。

entries.definition: The scientific field that studies clocks and rhythms; it is a discipline, not a body part.
entries.definitionCN: 研究钟与节律的科学领域；是学科，不是身体部件。

entries.definition: A broad phrase for any inner timing sense, used of animals and even of machines.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何内部计时感，可用于动物，甚至机器。

entries.definition: The structure that sets the rhythm, especially the suprachiasmatic nucleus or the heart's sinoatrial node.
entries.definitionCN: 设定节律的结构，尤指视交叉上核或心脏窦房结。

entries.definition: A person or mechanism that records time; in biology it names the clock component that sets the pace.
entries.definitionCN: 记录时间的人或装置；在生物学中指设定节拍的钟组件。

entries.definition: A popular term for supposed regular cycles in mood or energy; it lacks the precision of biological clock.
entries.definitionCN: 通俗术语，指情绪或精力上被认为存在的规律周期；不如 biological clock 精确。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Biology is Greek for 'life-study'; clock is a time machine: a time machine built into a living body.
normal.cn: biology 是希腊语「研究生命」；clock 是计时机器：一台装进活身体里的计时机器。

normal.en: The family runs biology, biological, clock, clockwork, and the phrase body clock.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 biology、biological、clock、clockwork，以及短语 body clock。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: reset the biological clock, biological clock gene, the clock is ticking.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：重置生物钟、生物钟基因、时钟在走。

normal.en: Morning light is the daily hand that winds the clock back to local time.
normal.cn: 清晨的光就是每天把钟拨回当地时间的那只手。

normal.en: The fertility sense is a metaphor, not physiology: the clock that ticks here is a deadline.
normal.cn: 生育义是比喻而非生理学：这里滴答走的钟是一个截止期限。

abstract.en: Picture a watch buried in the body, still ticking with no one to wind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只埋进身体的表，无人上弦却仍在走。

abstract.en: Picture a sundial indoors, corrected every morning by a window.
abstract.cn: 想象一只放在室内的日晷，每天早晨靠一扇窗来校正。

abstract.en: Picture an hourglass in the blood, its sand always falling.
abstract.cn: 想象血液里有一只沙漏，沙一直在落。

examples.en: A shift worker's biological clock rarely adjusts to a changing roster.
examples.cn: 换班工人的生物钟很难适应不断变动的排班。

examples.en: Morning light resets the biological clock after a late night.
examples.cn: 清晨的光在熬夜之后重置生物钟。

examples.en: She felt her biological clock ticking and changed her plans.
examples.cn: 她感觉自己的生育时钟在走，于是改变了计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「生物 + 钟」——身体里装着一只不用上弦的钟 → 生物钟

root: biological 由希腊 bios「生命」+ -logia「学问」构成；clock 经中古荷兰语来自中世纪拉丁 clocca「钟」。英语短语 biological clock。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object: a timepiece inside a living body. The object is first the whole system, then the tissue, its genes, its setting, its failures, and finally the popular deadline it resembles.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个物件展开：活身体里的一只计时器。这个物件先是整套系统，再是组织、基因、对时、失灵，最后是它所比拟的通俗期限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old pocket watch embedded in the body, running without a key and corrected by daylight.
core.cn: 核心意象：嵌在身体里的一只旧怀表，不用钥匙上弦，靠日光校正。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND SEAT: the whole capacity and the small tissue that generates it.
branches.cn: 系统与座位：整体能力，以及产生它的那一小簇组织。

branches.en: SOCIAL MEANING: the same phrase names a fertility deadline and a sense of urgency.
branches.cn: 社会含义：同一短语既指生育期限，也指紧迫感。

branches.en: MOLECULAR GEAR: genes and proteins are the gears of the timepiece.
branches.cn: 分子齿轮：基因与蛋白质是这只表的齿轮。

branches.en: SETTING AND BREAKING: daylight resets it, and a mismatched schedule breaks it.
branches.cn: 对表与损坏：日光重置它，错配的日程弄坏它。

branches.en: SEASONAL CALENDAR: the same system can be read across a year, not only a day.
branches.cn: 季节日历：同一套系统不仅能读一天，也能读一年。

intro.en: The phrase mixes a Greek-derived scientific word with a Germanic everyday noun, which is why it feels both technical and familiar.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊来源的科学词与日耳曼语系的日常名词混在一起，因此既技术又亲切。

latinIntro.en: Biology is Greek in both parts, with no Latin root. Clock descends from Medieval Latin clocca 'bell', probably of Celtic origin; that is the only Latin element in the phrase.
latinIntro.cn: biology 两部分都是希腊语，没有拉丁词根。clock 来自中世纪拉丁 clocca「钟」，可能源出凯尔特语；这是短语中唯一的拉丁成分。

definition_zh: 描写的；描述性的；说明性的
definition_en: giving an account of what something is like rather than judging or changing it
core_image: 一支笔沿着物体的轮廓慢慢走，把看到的形状写下来
scene: 这里指「描写的」。 The report gives a descriptive account of the village rather than a plan for improving it.
sceneCN: 这里 descriptive 是「描述性的」（第 1 个义项：说明是什么样，而不作评判或规划）；句意：这份报告对村庄作了描述性说明，而不是提出改善计划。图中可辨识物件：村庄全景、记录板、笔、未标注改造方案的空白页。

pos.zh: 描写的；描述性的；说明性的

senses.title: Saying what something is like
senses.titleCN: 描写的：说清它是什么样
senses.definition: giving an account of the features of something rather than evaluating it
senses.definitionCN: 说明某物的特征，而不是对它作出评价
senses.example: The guide is descriptive rather than judgemental about the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这本指南对这座小镇是描述性的，而不是评判性的。
senses.why: describere means 'to write down'. The -ive suffix marks the quality of writing something down as it is, without adding a verdict.
senses.whyCN: describere 意为“写下”。-ive 标记“照原样写下来”的性质，不额外加判断。

senses.title: Detailed and vivid
senses.titleCN: 描写生动的：细节多到能看见
senses.definition: giving a full and vivid picture through concrete details
senses.definitionCN: 通过具体细节给出完整而生动的画面
senses.example: Her descriptive paragraph made the market smell and sound real.
senses.exampleCN: 她那段描写让集市的气味和声音都变得真实。
senses.why: A good description writes down enough detail that the reader can reconstruct the scene. The suffix -ive turns that act into a quality of the text.
senses.whyCN: 好的描写写下的细节足够读者重建场景。-ive 把这一动作变成文本的性质。

senses.title: Linguistics: observing, not prescribing
senses.titleCN: 描写语言学的：只记录怎么说
senses.definition: in linguistics, based on how language is actually used rather than on rules about how it should be used
senses.definitionCN: 语言学上基于语言的实际使用，而不是规定应当如何使用
senses.example: Descriptive grammar records the forms speakers actually use.
senses.exampleCN: 描写语法记录说话者实际使用的形式。
senses.why: The contrast with prescriptive is exact: one writes language down as observed, the other writes rules in advance. The root scribere holds both.
senses.whyCN: 它与 prescriptive 的对比非常精确：一个照观察写下语言，一个预先立规。词根 scribere 同时支撑两者。

senses.title: Statistics that summarise data
senses.titleCN: 描述统计：只把数据的样子说出来
senses.definition: in statistics, summarising the main features of a data set without drawing conclusions beyond it
senses.definitionCN: 统计学上概括数据的主要特征，而不超出数据作结论
senses.example: Descriptive statistics showed a mean age of thirty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 描述统计显示平均年龄为三十二岁。
senses.why: The numbers describe the sample instead of testing a hypothesis about the population. The adjective keeps the 'write down what is there' stance.
senses.whyCN: 这些数字描述样本，而不是检验关于总体的假设。这个形容词保持了“把存在的写下来”的立场。

senses.title: Characteristic of something
senses.titleCN: 体现……特征的：这个词就说明它
senses.definition: used with 'of' to say that a word or feature characterises something
senses.definitionCN: 与 of 连用，表示某个词或特征体现了某事物的特点
senses.example: The term 'coastal' is descriptive of the region's economy.
senses.exampleCN: coastal 这个词体现了该地区经济的特点。
senses.why: Here the showing turns into representing: the label describes the thing so well that it becomes a characteristic rather than a comment.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“显示”转为“代表”：标签把事物描述得如此贴切，以致成为特征而不是评论。

senses.title: Merely labelling
senses.titleCN: 仅作标识的：名字只告诉你它是什么
senses.definition: naming or classifying something without explaining or justifying it
senses.definitionCN: 只给某物命名或分类，而不解释或论证
senses.example: The title is descriptive only; it makes no claim about quality.
senses.exampleCN: 这个标题只是标识性的，并不对质量作任何主张。
senses.why: A descriptive name writes down what is visible and stops there. The word marks the boundary between naming and evaluating.
senses.whyCN: 描述性名称只写下看得见的东西，到此为止。这个词标记了命名与评价之间的界线。

senses.title: Technical drawing
senses.titleCN: 画法几何的：用图把形状说清
senses.definition: in descriptive geometry, relating to the accurate two-dimensional representation of three-dimensional objects
senses.definitionCN: 画法几何中，用二维图形准确表示三维物体的
senses.example: Descriptive geometry is still taught to engineering students.
senses.exampleCN: 工程专业学生仍要学画法几何。
senses.why: Drawing an object's edges on paper is literally writing it down in lines. The technical sense is the oldest physical meaning of describere.
senses.whyCN: 把物体轮廓画在纸上，字面上就是用线条写下来。这个技术义是 describere 最古老的物理含义。

senses.title: Observational research
senses.titleCN: 描述性研究：先看清，再解释
senses.definition: in research, describing a situation or population without testing causal claims
senses.definitionCN: 研究中描述某种状况或人群，而不检验因果主张
senses.example: The study is descriptive and does not prove that the two events are linked.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究是描述性的，并不能证明两个事件有关联。
senses.why: A descriptive study records what is observed before asking why. The adjective signals that no causal claim has been written into the record.
senses.whyCN: 描述性研究在追问原因之前先记录观察到的内容。这个形容词表明记录里没有写进因果主张。

intro.en: Descriptive comes from Latin describere 'to write down, copy off', de- 'down' plus scribere 'write'. English formed the adjective with -ive; the contrast with prescriptive became central in linguistics.
intro.cn: descriptive 来自拉丁 describere“写下、描摹”，由 de-“向下”和 scribere“写”构成。英语用 -ive 构成形容词；与 prescriptive 的对立在语言学中变得关键。

items.en: scribere meant 'to write, mark, draw'. It is the source of script, scribe, prescribe, subscribe and manuscript, so the whole family concerns writing.
items.cn: scribere 意为“写、标记、画”。它是 script、scribe、prescribe、subscribe、manuscript 的来源，整个词族都与书写有关。

items.en: describere adds de- 'down', giving 'to write down, copy off, delineate'. Latin used it for drawing a boundary as well as for describing in words.
items.cn: describere 加 de-“向下”，意为“写下、描摹、画出轮廓”。拉丁语既用它表示划界，也表示用文字描述。

items.en: English forms descriptive on the stem descript- plus -ive in the 16th century. The exact first record is uncertain because description and descriptive entered close together.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪以 descript- 词干加 -ive 构成 descriptive。由于 description 与 descriptive 进入时间相近，确切最早记录存疑。

items.en: Descriptive geometry was named in the 18th century for the drawing of solid forms on flat paper, reviving the literal 'draw a boundary' sense.
items.cn: 画法几何在 18 世纪得名，指在平面上绘制立体形状，复活了字面的“画出轮廓”义。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries, descriptive became the opposite of prescriptive: record usage versus lay down rules. The pair is now standard in language teaching.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，descriptive 成为 prescriptive 的对立面：记录用法对立法定规则。这一对词如今是语言教学的标准术语。

items.en: Descriptive statistics was fixed in the 20th century for summaries of a sample. The word marks what the numbers do: they describe, they do not test.
items.cn: 描述统计在 20 世纪固定下来，指对样本的概括。这个词标记数字的功能：它们描述，而不检验。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the scrib- stem; the near-meaning group distinguishes describing, illustrating, observing and prescribing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 scrib- 词干；近义组区分描述、说明、观察与规定。

entries.definition: to say what something is like; the verb names the act of writing down.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物是什么样；这个动词命名“写下”的动作。

entries.definition: a spoken or written account; it is the thing produced by describing.
entries.definitionCN: 口头或书面的描述；它是描述动作产生的成品。

entries.definition: laying down rules about what should be done or used; the direct opposite of descriptive in linguistics.
entries.definitionCN: 规定应当如何做或如何使用；在语言学中是 descriptive 的直接对立面。

entries.definition: containing many specific facts; it stresses quantity of detail, while descriptive stresses the act of depicting.
entries.definitionCN: 包含许多具体事实；它强调细节数量，而 descriptive 强调描绘动作。

entries.definition: serving to explain by example or picture; it aims at understanding, while descriptive aims at an accurate account.
entries.definitionCN: 通过例子或图片说明；它追求理解，而 descriptive 追求准确叙述。

entries.definition: based on watching without intervention; it is the methodological cousin of descriptive research.
entries.definitionCN: 基于观察而不干预；它是描述性研究在方法上的表亲。

entries.definition: conveying feeling or personal style; descriptive conveys facts, expressive conveys the writer's response.
entries.definitionCN: 传达感情或个人风格；descriptive 传达事实，expressive 传达作者的反应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'down' + scribere 'write': descriptive text is written down from observation.
normal.cn: de-“向下”+ scribere“写”：描述性文本是从观察中写下来的。

normal.en: Remember descriptive versus prescriptive as a pair: observe and record, or command and correct.
normal.cn: 把 descriptive 与 prescriptive 成对记：观察记录，或命令纠正。

normal.en: In statistics, descriptive numbers summarise; inferential numbers test. The adjective tells you which job is being done.
normal.cn: 统计中，描述性数字做概括；推断性数字做检验。这个形容词告诉你正在做哪件事。

normal.en: A descriptive title tells you what the thing is, not whether it is good.
normal.cn: 描述性标题告诉你它是什么，而不是它好不好。

normal.en: descriptive geometry is literally drawing an object on paper, the oldest sense of the root.
normal.cn: 画法几何字面上就是把物体画在纸上，是词根最古老的义项。

abstract.en: Think of a pencil tracing the outline of a cup without shading it or grading its design.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔只沿着杯子轮廓走，不上阴影，也不评价设计。

abstract.en: Think of a nature documentary that names and shows the animal without telling you what to think.
abstract.cn: 想象一部自然纪录片，只命名并展示动物，不告诉你怎么想。

abstract.en: Think of a map that draws the coastline exactly as it is, leaving the traveller to choose the route.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图如实画出海岸线，把选路的自由留给旅人。

examples.en: The manual is descriptive, so it tells you how the machine behaves rather than how to fix it.
examples.cn: 这本手册是描述性的，讲的是机器如何运作，而不是如何修理。

examples.en: Her descriptive writing brings the old harbour back to life.
examples.cn: 她的描写性写作让旧港重现生机。

examples.en: The chart provides descriptive statistics for each age group.
examples.cn: 这张图表提供了各年龄组的描述统计。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地scribe体”——地（de）上拿笔（scribe）照着东西写，只写看到的不加评价 → descriptive 描述性的

root: 拉丁 describere“写下、描摹”（de-“向下”+ scribere“写”）；descript- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one stance: the writer records what is there, and stops before judging or commanding.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个立场：写作者记录存在之物，在评判或命令之前停手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pencil tracing the outline of an object exactly as it stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：铅笔沿着物体原样描出轮廓。

branches.en: VIVIDNESS: a detailed scene is the same writing-down at a higher level of resolution.
branches.cn: 生动：细节场景是同一种“写下”在高分辨率层级上。

branches.en: OBSERVATION AS METHOD: descriptive linguistics and descriptive research both record usage or behaviour without imposing a rule.
branches.cn: 观察作为方法：描写语言学与描述性研究都记录用法或行为，不强加规则。

branches.en: SUMMARISING AND DRAWING: statistical summaries and technical drawings both reduce a complex object to a faithful outline.
branches.cn: 概括与绘图：统计概括与技术制图都把复杂对象缩减为忠实的轮廓。

branches.en: CHARACTERISING AND LABELLING: a word descriptive of a region and a merely descriptive title both stop at identification.
branches.cn: 特征与标识：描述地区特征的词与仅作标识的标题，都停在识别层面。

branches.en: THE BASE STANCE: all extensions keep the refusal to prescribe, even when the description is reduced to a single number or line.
branches.cn: 基础立场：所有引申都保留“不作规定”的态度，即使描述被缩减为一个数字或一条线。

intro.en: Descriptive is descript- plus -ive. The Latin de- and scribere are fused; English productively uses -ive, -ion, -ively and -iveness around this stem.
intro.cn: descriptive 是 descript- 加 -ive。拉丁 de- 与 scribere 已融合；英语在这个词干周围能产地使用 -ive、-ion、-ively、-iveness。

latinIntro.en: Latin scribere 'to write' yields describere 'write down', descriptio 'a description', and scriptum 'something written'. English relatives include describe, description, prescribe, subscribe and manuscript.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 scribere“写”派生 describere“写下”、descriptio“描述”、scriptum“写下的东西”。英语同族词包括 describe、description、prescribe、subscribe、manuscript。

items.meaning: to write down; to say what something is like
items.example: The witness described the car in detail.
items.exampleCN: 证人详细描述了那辆车。

items.meaningCN: 描述；说明（-ion 构成结果名词）
items.example: The job description lists the main duties.
items.exampleCN: 职位说明列出了主要职责。

items.meaningCN: 描述性的；描写的（-ive 构成形容词）
描述性地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The term is used descriptively, not as criticism.
items.exampleCN: 这个说法是描述性用法，不是批评。

items.meaningCN: 描述性；描写性（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The descriptiveness of the diary makes it valuable to historians.
items.exampleCN: 这本日记的描写性使它对历史学家很有价值。

items.meaningCN: 规定；开处方（pre-“预先”+ scribere“写”）
items.example: The law prescribes a minimum age for the licence.
items.exampleCN: 法律规定该驾照的最低年龄。

items.meaning: to write one's name under; to agree to receive
items.example: She subscribed to two science magazines.
items.exampleCN: 她订阅了两本科学杂志。

items.meaningCN: 手稿（manu-“手”+ scriptum“写下的东西”）
items.example: The manuscript was revised three times.

definition_zh: 适者生存；最适应环境者存活下来（常被简化传播的说法）
definition_en: the principle that individuals best adapted to their environment are most likely to survive and reproduce, a phrase often simplified into a slogan
core_image: 草原上一群羚羊奔逃，落后的一只被尘土吞没，远处的幼崽仍在吃草
scene: 草原上一群羚羊奔逃，落后的一只被尘土吞没，远处的幼崽仍在吃草。 In the wild, survival of the fittest is about leaving offspring, not about winning a fight.
sceneCN: 这里取第 4 个义项（「最适应」而非「最强」）；句意为在野外，适者生存讲的是留下后代，而不是打赢一场架。

pos.zh: 名词短语：适者生存；最适应环境者存活下来

collocations.phrase: the doctrine of survival of the fittest
a slogan of survival of the fittest
survival of the fittest in the market
a misuse of survival of the fittest
survival of the fittest among species
the phrase survival of the fittest

derivatives.zh: 由「适合的」加最高级词尾构成，义为「最适应的」
中古英语中义为「合适的、恰当的」，其更早来源不确定
由「适合的」加抽象名词词尾构成，义为「适应度；健康」
由「适合的」加比较级词尾构成，义为「更适应的」
由否定前缀加「适合的」构成，义为「不适合的」
由表示「错误」的前缀加「适合的」构成，义为「不适应者」

senses.title: A summary of natural selection
senses.definition: the principle that variants better suited to an environment leave more offspring
senses.definitionCN: 指更适应环境的变体留下更多后代这一原理
senses.example: Survival of the fittest summarises natural selection in five words.
senses.exampleCN: 「适者生存」用五个词概括了自然选择。
senses.why: The phrase compresses a long argument into a memorable formula, which is both its strength and its danger.
senses.whyCN: 这条短语把长篇论证压成一句易记的口号，这既是它的力量，也是它的危险。

senses.title: Spencer's coinage
senses.definition: the phrase coined by Herbert Spencer in the eighteen-sixties after reading Darwin
senses.definitionCN: 指赫伯特·斯宾塞在十九世纪六十年代读达尔文之后造出的说法
senses.example: The phrase survival of the fittest was coined by Herbert Spencer.
senses.exampleCN: 「适者生存」这一说法由赫伯特·斯宾塞造出。
senses.why: A philosopher of society supplied the words before the biologist adopted them.
senses.whyCN: 社会哲学家先提供了措辞，生物学家后来才采用。

senses.title: Darwin's adoption of the phrase
senses.titleCN: 达尔文对该短语的采用
senses.definition: the addition of the phrase to later editions of the Origin of Species as a synonym for natural selection
senses.definitionCN: 指达尔文在《物种起源》后来的版本中加入这条短语，作为自然选择的同义说法
senses.example: Darwin adopted survival of the fittest in the fifth edition.
senses.exampleCN: 达尔文在第五版中采用了「适者生存」。
senses.why: Readers remembered the slogan more easily than the argument, so Darwin took it over.
senses.whyCN: 读者更容易记住口号而不是论证，达尔文于是把它收为己用。

senses.title: Fittest meaning best adapted
senses.definition: the sense that fit means suited to local conditions, not muscular or aggressive
senses.definitionCN: 指「适合」意为适应本地条件，而非肌肉强壮或好斗
senses.example: Survival of the fittest does not mean survival of the strongest.
senses.exampleCN: 「适者生存」并不意味着最强者的生存。
senses.why: Fit is a relation between an organism and its surroundings, not a score in a fight.
senses.whyCN: 「适合」是生物与环境之间的关系，不是打斗的比分。

senses.title: The popular competitive misreading
senses.definition: the everyday use of the phrase to justify ruthless competition
senses.definitionCN: 指日常语言中用这条短语为无情竞争辩护
senses.example: The slogan survival of the fittest is often used to excuse ruthless competition.
senses.exampleCN: 「适者生存」这句口号常被用来为无情竞争开脱。
senses.why: A biological relation was turned into a social permission, and the turn is easy because the words sound like a race.
senses.whyCN: 一种生物关系被变成一种社会许可，这种转变之所以容易，是因为措辞听起来像一场赛跑。

senses.title: A business metaphor
senses.definition: the use of the phrase for firms competing and failing in a market
senses.definitionCN: 指用这条短语形容企业在市场中竞争与出局
senses.example: Executives invoke survival of the fittest to justify closures.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者援引「适者生存」为关厂辩护。
senses.why: Markets do select, but the selected unit is a firm, not a lineage, and the timescale is months, not generations.
senses.whyCN: 市场确实在选择，但被选择的单位是公司而非世系，时间尺度是几个月而非世代。

senses.title: Differential reproduction in ecology
senses.definition: the measurable version of the idea: which individuals leave the most surviving offspring
senses.definitionCN: 指这一想法的可测量版本：哪些个体留下最多存活后代
senses.example: Ecologists test survival of the fittest by counting offspring.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家通过清点后代来检验「适者生存」。
senses.why: To be science rather than slogan, the phrase must be turned into counts and comparisons.
senses.whyCN: 要成为科学而非口号，这条短语必须变成计数与比较。

senses.title: Its misuse as social doctrine
senses.definition: the extension of the phrase to justify class, racial or national hierarchy
senses.definitionCN: 指把这条短语扩展到为阶级、种族或民族等级辩护
senses.example: Social Darwinism stretched survival of the fittest far beyond biology.
senses.exampleCN: 社会达尔文主义把「适者生存」远远扩展到生物学之外。
senses.why: The borrowing looked scientific while dropping every condition that made the original claim testable.
senses.whyCN: 这种借用看似科学，却丢掉了使原命题可检验的每一个条件。

senses.title: A critique of the phrase's limits
senses.definition: the objection that the slogan hides cooperation, luck and inheritance
senses.definitionCN: 指批评这句口号掩盖了合作、运气与遗传的作用
senses.example: Critics say survival of the fittest says little about cooperation.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说「适者生存」几乎没谈到合作。
senses.why: What a slogan leaves out is often what a theory most needs to explain.
senses.whyCN: 口号省略的部分，往往正是理论最需要解释的部分。

intro.en: The phrase is not ancient: Herbert Spencer coined it in the eighteen-sixties after reading Darwin, and Darwin adopted it in the fifth edition of the Origin of Species in 1869. Fit is an English adjective meaning suitable, first recorded in Middle English, and its earlier origin is uncertain; the superlative ending makes fittest mean most suited, not strongest.
intro.cn: 这条短语并不古老：赫伯特·斯宾塞在十九世纪六十年代读达尔文之后造出它，达尔文在一八六九年《物种起源》第五版中采用。「适合的」是英语形容词，中古英语已有记录，其更早来源不确定；最高级词尾使「最适」意为最适合，而非最强。

items.en: The adjective meant suitable or proper; its earlier origin is uncertain, and no Latin source can be assumed.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为合适的、恰当的；其更早来源不确定，不能假定有拉丁语来源。

items.en: The superlative ending marks the highest degree of the quality.
items.cn: 这个最高级词尾标记性质的最高程度。

items.en: The first edition of the Origin argued for natural selection without using the slogan.
items.cn: 《物种起源》第一版论证自然选择，却没有使用这句口号。

items.en: Herbert Spencer coined the phrase in his biology, applying it to societies as well as organisms.
items.cn: 赫伯特·斯宾塞在其生物学著作中造出这条短语，并同时用于社会与生物。

items.en: Darwin added it to the fifth edition as a synonym, while Wallace disliked the substitution.
items.cn: 达尔文在第五版把它作为同义说法加入，而华莱士不喜欢这一替换。

items.en: The phrase spread as a slogan in business and politics, far from its original technical setting.
items.cn: 这条短语作为口号在商业与政治中传播，远离其原初的技术语境。

note.en: The first group shares the suitability word or a derived ending; the second group names the scientific concepts and the social misuse.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「适合」的词或派生词尾；第二组是科学概念与社会误用。

entries.definition: Suitable, in good condition, or a match of size and shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指合适的、健康的，或尺寸形状相合。

entries.definition: The superlative, most suited to the conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 最高级形式，指最适合条件。

entries.definition: The quality of being suitable, or good physical condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指适合的性质，或良好的体能。

entries.definition: Not suitable, or in poor condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指不适合的，或状态不佳的。

entries.definition: A person or thing that does not fit its surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 指与环境不合的人或物。

entries.definition: The process the phrase tries to summarise.
entries.definitionCN: 指这条短语试图概括的过程。

entries.definition: A trait that improves survival or reproduction in a setting.
entries.definitionCN: 指在特定环境中改善存活或繁殖的性状。

entries.definition: In biology, the relative contribution to future generations.
entries.definitionCN: 生物学中指对未来世代的相对贡献。

entries.definition: Unequal survival among variants, the measurable core of the idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指变体之间不相等的存活，是这一想法的可测核心。

entries.definition: The misuse of biological selection to justify social hierarchy.
entries.definitionCN: 指把生物选择误用于为社会等级辩护。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations separate the phrase's three parts: who survives, what fit means, and who coined it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把短语分成三块：谁存活、「适合」指什么、以及是谁造的。

normal.en: Spencer coined it, Darwin adopted it, and Wallace disliked it.
normal.cn: 斯宾塞造出它，达尔文采用它，华莱士不喜欢它。

normal.en: Fit means suited to the place, not muscular or aggressive.
normal.cn: 「适合」指适应某地，而不是强壮或好斗。

normal.en: Success is measured in surviving offspring, not in victories.
normal.cn: 成功以存活后代来衡量，而不是以胜场。

normal.en: A firm is not a species, and a quarter is not a generation.
normal.cn: 公司不是物种，一个季度也不是一个世代。

normal.en: The slogan travels further than the theory because it is shorter.
normal.cn: 口号比理论传播得更远，因为它更短。

abstract.en: A memorable phrase can outrun the argument that gave it meaning.
abstract.cn: 一句易记的话，能跑得比赋予它意义的论证更远。

abstract.en: Selection is a relation to a place, not a ranking of strength.
abstract.cn: 选择是与某地的关系，而不是力量的排名。

abstract.en: Every slogan is a theory with its conditions stripped away.
abstract.cn: 每一句口号都是被剥掉条件的理论。

examples.en: Survival of the fittest is often printed on posters beside a picture of a race.
examples.cn: 「适者生存」常被印在海报上，旁边配一幅赛跑图。

examples.en: The phrase survival of the fittest entered biology through Spencer, not through Darwin's first edition.
examples.cn: 「适者生存」经由斯宾塞进入生物学，而不是通过达尔文的第一版。

examples.en: A market crash is not survival of the fittest in any biological sense.
examples.cn: 市场崩盘在任何生物学意义上都不是「适者生存」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「色外涡·欧夫·则·菲泰斯特」——活下来的是最「合身」的那个，不是最壮的那个：适者生存

root: 短语由十九世纪六十年代的斯宾塞造出，达尔文于一八六九年第五版采用；其中「适合的」是中古英语形容词，更早来源不确定，最高级词尾表示「最适合」，与「最强」无关。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow the phrase from its compressed scientific meaning to its coinage, Darwin's adoption, the true sense of fit, the popular misreading, the business metaphor, the ecological measure, the social misuse and the critique.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从被压缩的科学含义出发，走向它的造语、达尔文的采用、「适合」的真正含义、流行误读、商业比喻、生态测量、社会误用与批评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: antelopes running, the laggard swallowed by dust, while a calf keeps grazing far off.
core.cn: 核心意象：羚羊奔逃，落后的一只被尘土吞没，远处的幼崽仍在吃草。

branches.en: THE MECHANISM AND ITS MEASURE: natural selection compressed, and the offspring counts that test it.
branches.cn: 机制与测量：被压缩的自然选择，以及检验它的后代计数。

branches.en: THE AUTHORSHIP: Spencer's coinage and Darwin's later adoption.
branches.cn: 作者：斯宾塞的造语与达尔文后来的采用。

branches.en: WHAT FIT MEANS: suited to local conditions, not strongest.
branches.cn: 「适合」的含义：适应本地条件，而非最强。

branches.en: THE POPULAR AND COMMERCIAL USES: an excuse for competition, and a market metaphor.
branches.cn: 流行与商业用法：为竞争开脱，以及市场比喻。

branches.en: THE MISUSE AND THE CRITIQUE: social hierarchy dressed as biology, and what the slogan hides.
branches.cn: 误用与批评：披着生物学外衣的社会等级，以及口号所掩盖的东西。

intro.en: The phrase is plain English grammar around one adjective: survival, of, the, fittest.
intro.cn: 这条短语是一个形容词加上普通的英语语法成分：生存、的、最、适合的。

latinIntro.en: Only survival has a Latin ancestry; the adjective fit is English, and its earlier source is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 只有「生存」有拉丁语祖先；形容词「适合的」是英语词，其更早来源不确定。

items.example: The word is about relation, not strength.
items.exampleCN: 这个词关乎关系，而非力量。

items.example: It supplies the first noun of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供短语的第一个名词。

items.example: It links survival to the group that survives.
items.exampleCN: 它把「存活」与存活的群体连接起来。

items.example: It makes fittest refer to a class rather than a person.
items.exampleCN: 它使「最适者」指一类而非某个人。

items.example: It underlies survival through the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: 它经拉丁动词支撑「生存」一词。

items.example: It forms survival from the verb.

中古英语义为「合适的」，更早来源不确定
由「适合的」加抽象名词词尾构成，义为「适应度」
由「适合的」加比较级词尾构成，义为「更适应的」

由表示「错误」的前缀加「适合的」构成，义为「不适应者」

definition_zh: 可读的；易读的；字迹清晰的；值得一读的
definition_en: able to be read easily, either because the marks are clear or the writing holds attention
core_image: 一页字迹工整的稿纸，灯再暗也不用凑近去认
scene: 灯下那封信的字迹清楚，连最小的注脚都一眼能认出。 The letter was readable even in the dim light of the lamp.
sceneCN: 这里 readable 指字迹清晰的、可读的（第 1 个义项：字迹可辨认）；句意为灯下那封信的字迹清楚，连最小的注脚都一眼能认出。

pos.zh: 可读的；易读的；字迹清晰的；值得一读的

senses.title: Clear enough to read
senses.definition: written or printed so clearly that the marks can be recognised without effort
senses.definitionCN: 书写或印刷得清楚，不用费力就能辨认
senses.example: Her readable handwriting made the marginal notes easy to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 她清晰的字迹让页边批注很容易跟上。
senses.why: This is the sense about the eye: the page asks nothing of the reader.
senses.whyCN: 这一层讲的是眼睛：纸页不向读者提任何要求。

senses.title: Worth reading
senses.titleCN: 值得一读的；引人入胜的
senses.definition: written in a way that holds a reader's attention and makes the time pass easily
senses.definitionCN: 写得能抓住读者注意力，让时间轻易过去
senses.example: The history was readable enough to finish on a train.
senses.exampleCN: 那本历史书写得够好读，一趟火车就能看完。
senses.why: Here the praise is for style and interest, not for the clarity of the marks.
senses.whyCN: 这一层赞的是文风和趣味，而不是笔迹有多清楚。

intro.en: Readable joins read, from Old English raedan, 'to interpret marks', with the ending -able.
intro.cn: readable 把 read（古英语 raedan，解读符号）与词尾 -able 组合起来。

items.en: Raedan meant to interpret or advise as well as to read.
items.cn: raedan 既指阅读，也指解读与劝告。

items.en: Read narrowed to the handling of written marks.
items.cn: read 后来收窄为处理书面符号。

items.en: The ending marks what can be done with ease.
items.cn: 词尾标记「可以顺利做到」。

items.en: Cheap printing made readable a selling word.
items.cn: 廉价印刷让 readable 成为卖点词。

items.en: Today it also judges screens, signs and code.
items.cn: 今天它也评判屏幕、标识与代码。

note.en: The look-alike group is the read- family; the near-meaning group separates legible, lucid, gripping and comprehensible.
note.cn: 形近组是 read 词族；近义组把「可辨认的」「清晰的」「引人入胜的」「可理解的」分开。

entries.definition: to interpret written marks.
entries.definitionCN: 解读书面符号。

entries.definition: a person who reads.
entries.definitionCN: 阅读的人。

entries.definition: the act or a measurement taken.
entries.definitionCN: 阅读行为或读得的数值。

entries.definition: without hesitation.
entries.definitionCN: 毫不迟疑地。

entries.definition: clear enough to be deciphered.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚到能被辨认的。

entries.definition: expressed with great clarity.
entries.definitionCN: 表达得极为清晰的。

entries.definition: holding attention strongly.
entries.definitionCN: 牢牢抓住注意力的。

entries.definition: able to be understood.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被理解的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a page that asks nothing of the eye.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一页不向眼睛提任何要求」的画面。

normal.en: Readable is read plus able: reading costs nothing extra.
normal.cn: readable 是 read 加 able：阅读不必多付力气。

normal.en: Picture a page you can skim in bad light.
normal.cn: 想象一页在昏暗光线下也能略读过去的纸。

normal.en: Say REE-duh-bl; it sounds like something already open.
normal.cn: 读 REE-duh-bl，听起来像已经翻开的东西。

normal.en: The word judges two things: marks and momentum.
normal.cn: 这个词评判两样东西：符号与推进力。

normal.en: Ask readable to whom: a child, a scanner, a tired commuter?
normal.cn: 问对谁可读：孩子、扫描仪，还是疲惫的通勤者？

abstract.en: Readable is a courtesy paid by the writer to the stranger.
abstract.cn: readable 是写作者付给陌生人的一份礼貌。

abstract.en: Clarity and interest are different debts: one is owed to the eye, the other to time.
abstract.cn: 清晰与有趣是两笔不同的债：一笔欠眼睛，一笔欠时间。

abstract.en: What is readable survives copying; what is merely legible does not.
abstract.cn: 可读的东西经得起传抄，仅仅可辨的东西不行。

examples.en: Her readable handwriting made the marginal notes easy to follow.
examples.cn: 她清晰的字迹让页边批注很容易跟上。

examples.en: The history was readable enough to finish on a train.
examples.cn: 那本历史书写得够好读，一趟火车就能看完。

examples.en: Readable code saves more time than clever code.
examples.cn: 可读的代码比聪明的代码省下更多时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: read（读）+ able（能）→ 读得下去的。

root: 古英语 raedan（解读）+ -able

sensesIntro.en: Readable has two senses: clear marks, and writing interesting enough to carry a reader.
sensesIntro.cn: readable 有两层：清楚可辨的字迹，以及有趣到能带着读者走的文字。

core.en: A PAGE THAT ASKS NOTHING OF THE EYE
core.cn: 一页不向眼睛提要求的纸

branches.en: Ink clear enough for any eye.
branches.cn: 任何眼睛都能看清的墨迹。

branches.en: A text that holds a commuter to the end.
branches.cn: 让通勤者读到最后一页的文字。

branches.en: Clarity for the eye, interest for the time.
branches.cn: 给眼睛的清晰，给时间的趣味。

branches.en: A page read in bad light.
branches.cn: 在坏光线下也能读的一页。

branches.en: Style as a courtesy to the stranger.
branches.cn: 作为给陌生人的礼貌的文风。

intro.en: The read- family is about interpretation: read, reader, readable and readability all describe someone making sense of marks.
intro.cn: read 词族讲的是解读：read、reader、readable、readability 都描述有人把符号弄明白。

latinIntro.en: Old English raedan gives the verb; the -able ending came through French from Latin -abilis, 'fit to be'.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 raedan 提供动词；-able 词尾经法语来自拉丁语 -abilis，意为「可以被……的」。
