how easy a text is to read

definition_zh: 派生的；缺乏原创的；衍生物；金融衍生品；（数学）导数
definition_en: derived from something else; lacking originality; or a thing produced from another source
core_image: 一条小溪从大河旁边分出去，水还是那批水，河道却是新的
scene: 实验室里，柳树皮中的化合物被改造成新药： The new drug is a derivative of a compound found in willow bark.
sceneCN: 这里 derivative 是「衍生物」（第 4 个义项：由另一物质经改造而来）；句意：这种新药是柳树皮中一种化合物的衍生物。图中可辨识物件：柳树皮、实验烧瓶、分子结构图、药片。

pos.zh: 派生的；由……衍生的；缺乏原创的
衍生物；衍生品；派生词；导数

collocations.zh: 缺乏原创性的；高度模仿的

senses.title: Coming from another source
senses.definition: formed or developed from something else rather than existing independently
senses.definitionCN: 由他物形成或发展而来，而非独立存在的
senses.example: The design is derivative of an earlier bridge in the same city.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计是从同城一座更早的桥派生出来的。
senses.why: derivare means 'to lead water away from a stream'. A derivative thing is water led off from an existing channel: it flows, but the source is not its own.
senses.whyCN: derivare 意为“从溪流引走水”。derivative 的东西就是从既有水道引出的水：它流动，但源头不属于自己。

senses.title: Lacking originality
senses.titleCN: 缺乏原创的：只是别人的回声
senses.definition: imitative and unoriginal, repeating ideas already used by others
senses.definitionCN: 模仿他人、缺乏原创，重复已有观念
senses.example: Critics called the sequel derivative and predictable.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称这部续集缺乏原创、一猜就中。
senses.why: The pejorative sense extends the same image: if everything is led off from another stream, nothing here has its own spring. The word judges the absence of an independent source.
senses.whyCN: 贬义义项是同一意象的延伸：如果一切都从别人的溪流引来，这里就没有自己的泉眼。这个词评判的正是独立源头的缺席。

senses.title: A financial instrument
senses.titleCN: 金融衍生品：价值挂在别的东西上
senses.definition: a financial contract whose value depends on an underlying asset, rate or index
senses.definitionCN: 价值取决于标的资产、利率或指数的金融合约
senses.example: The fund used interest-rate derivatives to hedge its loans.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金用利率衍生品为贷款做对冲。
senses.why: The contract has no independent value; it is led off from a bond, a rate or a price. Finance chose the word because the value literally flows from the underlying.
senses.whyCN: 这种合约没有独立价值，它的价值从债券、利率或价格引出。金融界用这个词，是因为价值确实来自标的。

senses.title: A chemical compound made from another
senses.titleCN: 化学衍生物：改一处就成了新物质
senses.definition: a substance obtained from another by a chemical change, often sharing its core structure
senses.definitionCN: 经化学变化从另一物质得到的物质，通常共享核心结构
senses.example: The derivative is more soluble than the original compound.
senses.exampleCN: 这种衍生物比原化合物更易溶解。
senses.why: Chemists modify one group and keep the skeleton, so the new molecule is a channel led off the old one. The stem is shared; only the branch differs.
senses.whyCN: 化学家改动一个基团、保留骨架，于是新分子就是从旧分子引出的水道。主干共享，只有分支不同。

senses.title: A word formed from another
senses.titleCN: 派生词：从词根长出来的新词
senses.definition: in linguistics, a word formed from an existing word or root by adding affixes or changing its form
senses.definitionCN: 语言学上由既有词或词根加词缀、改变形式而形成的新词
senses.example: The noun 'kindness' is a derivative of the adjective 'kind'.
senses.exampleCN: 名词 kindness 是形容词 kind 的派生词。
senses.why: Word formation is treated as water led from a source: the root supplies the meaning and the suffix opens a new channel, producing a new word.
senses.whyCN: 构词被看成从源头引水：词根提供意义，后缀开出新水道，产生新词。

senses.title: The rate of change in calculus
senses.definition: in mathematics, the rate at which a function changes with respect to one of its variables
senses.definitionCN: 数学中函数相对于某个变量的变化率
senses.example: The derivative of a straight line's position is its constant speed.
senses.exampleCN: 直线运动的位移导数是其恒定速度。
senses.why: A derivative is a value drawn out of a function by a limiting process. The word keeps the sense of something obtained from a larger source, not invented independently.
senses.whyCN: 导数是经极限过程从函数中引出的值。这个词保留了“从更大源头取得而非独立发明”的含义。

senses.title: A work adapted from another
senses.titleCN: 演绎作品：在原作上再创作
senses.definition: in copyright law, a work that adapts or transforms an existing protected work
senses.definitionCN: 版权法中改编或转化既有受保护作品的新作品
senses.example: The film is a derivative work based on a 19th-century novel.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影是改编自一部 19 世纪小说的演绎作品。
senses.why: Copyright uses the image precisely: the new work draws its substance from the old one, so permission flows with the water.
senses.whyCN: 版权法精确使用了这个意象：新作品从旧作品取得实质内容，因此许可随水一起流动。

senses.title: A secondary product of research
senses.titleCN: 副产品：主流程之外长出来的结果
senses.definition: something produced as a secondary result of a process, project or discovery
senses.definitionCN: 作为某过程、项目或发现的次要结果而产生的东西
senses.example: A useful battery material emerged as a derivative of the space programme.
senses.exampleCN: 一种有用的电池材料作为航天计划的衍生成果出现。
senses.why: Here the source is a process rather than a substance. The result is still led off the main channel, which is why it counts as a derivative rather than a primary product.
senses.whyCN: 这里的源头是过程而不是物质。结果仍从主水道引出，因此算衍生物而不是主产品。

intro.en: Derivative comes from Latin derivare 'to lead water away from a stream', de- 'from' plus rivus 'stream'. English first used it for 'derived things', then for chemistry, linguistics and mathematics; the financial sense is 20th-century.
intro.cn: derivative 来自拉丁 derivare“从溪流引走水”，由 de-“从”和 rivus“溪流”构成。英语最初用它表示“派生之物”，后来用于化学、语言学和数学；金融义是 20 世纪的产物。

items.en: rivus meant 'a small stream or channel'. It also gave English river and rival, the latter from rivalis 'one who uses the same stream'.
items.cn: rivus 意为“小溪、水道”。它也派生了英语 river 和 rival，后者来自 rivalis“共用同一条溪流的人”。

items.en: derivare 'to lead off water' is de- 'from' plus rivare 'to channel'. The literal operation is engineering: a branch canal takes water from a main stream.
items.cn: derivare“引走水”是 de-“从”加 rivare“开渠”。字面操作是工程性的：支渠从主溪流取水。

items.en: Old French deriver passed the verb into English as derive. The adjective and noun derivative followed in the 16th century; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语 deriver 把动词以 derive 形式传给英语。形容词与名词 derivative 在 16 世纪跟进，确切最早年代存疑。

items.en: In the 19th century chemistry named a compound made by modifying another as a derivative. The shared skeleton is the main stream, and the change is the branch.
items.cn: 19 世纪化学把经改造另一化合物而得到的物质称为 derivative。共享的骨架是主溪流，改动则是支渠。

items.en: Linguistics applies the term to words formed from roots or other words. A root supplies meaning, and affixes open a new channel.
items.cn: 语言学用该词指由词根或其他词形成的词。词根提供意义，词缀开出新水道。

items.en: Financial derivatives appear in the 20th century. Their value is explicitly derived from an underlying asset, so the metaphor became a definition.
items.cn: 金融衍生品出现于 20 世纪。其价值明确来自标的资产，于是隐喻变成了定义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the derive family and different endings; the near-meaning group separates copied, secondary and mathematically derived things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 derive 词族、词尾不同；近义组区分模仿的、次要的和数学上派生的事物。

entries.definition: to obtain from a source; to originate. It names the act of leading something off, while derivative names the result.
entries.definitionCN: 从某来源获得；起源于。它命名引出动作，而 derivative 命名结果。

entries.definition: the process of deriving, or the origin of a word; the -ation suffix focuses on the process rather than the product.
entries.definitionCN: 推导过程；词源。-ation 后缀聚焦过程而不是产物。

entries.definition: relating to word formation; a derivational affix creates a new word rather than a new grammatical form.
entries.definitionCN: 构词方面的；派生词缀创造新词，而不是新的语法形式。

entries.definition: copying the style or behaviour of others; close to the pejorative sense of derivative, but stresses copying as an act.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿他人风格或行为的；接近 derivative 的贬义，但强调“模仿”这一动作。

entries.definition: coming after or depending on something primary; derivative stresses the source, secondary stresses the rank.
entries.definitionCN: 次要的；在首要事物之后或依赖其存在；derivative 强调来源，secondary 强调等级。

entries.definition: a secondary result of a process; closest to sense 8, but it does not imply that the substance was deliberately derived.
entries.definitionCN: 过程的次要结果；最接近第 8 义，但不暗示该物质是被有意衍生出来的。

entries.definition: a thing that develops from a larger one, like a branch from a stem; it is figurative and less technical than derivative.
entries.definitionCN: 从较大事物发展出来的分支，如同主干上的枝条；它更形象，技术性不如 derivative。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'from' + rivus 'stream': a derivative is water led off from another stream.
normal.cn: de-“从”+ rivus“溪流”：derivative 就是从另一条溪流引出的水。

normal.en: river and rival are cousins from rivus: the rival is the person who shares your stream.
normal.cn: river 和 rival 都是 rivus 的表亲：rival 就是与你共用一条溪流的人。

normal.en: In mathematics, look for the pattern f'(x): the prime mark is the sign that a value has been drawn from the function.
normal.cn: 数学里找 f'(x) 这个写法：撇号就是“从函数中引出值”的标志。

normal.en: The financial phrase is derivative contract; if the value depends on something else, it is a derivative.
normal.cn: 金融搭配是 derivative contract；如果价值取决于别的东西，它就是衍生品。

normal.en: A derivative work in copyright is an adaptation, which is why the same word appears in film and software licences.
normal.cn: 版权中的 derivative work 是改编作品，所以同一个词会出现在电影和软件许可里。

abstract.en: Think of a garden hose split by a Y-connector: the second line carries the same water.
abstract.cn: 想象一根花园水管被 Y 形接头分开：第二条管里流的是同一批水。

abstract.en: Think of a river delta: every channel is the main river redistributed, not a new river.
abstract.cn: 想象一片河口三角洲：每条水道都是主河的重分，而不是一条新河。

abstract.en: Think of a cover song: the melody is borrowed, the performance is new, and both facts matter.
abstract.cn: 想象一首翻唱歌曲：旋律是借来的，演绎是新的，两个事实都重要。

examples.en: Many modern drugs are derivatives of plants used in traditional medicine.
examples.cn: 许多现代药物是传统医学中所用植物的衍生物。

examples.en: The bank lost heavily on derivatives tied to mortgage debt.
examples.cn: 这家银行在与房贷债务挂钩的衍生品上损失惨重。

examples.en: His early paintings are derivative, but the later work has its own voice.
examples.cn: 他早期的画缺乏原创，但后期作品有了自己的声音。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地river体”——地（de）上的 river（河流）分出一条小水道，就是它的衍生 → derivative 派生的、衍生物

root: 拉丁 derivare“从溪流引水”（de-“从”+ rivus“溪流”）；derivat- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one flow: something is led out of an existing channel, so its existence depends on a source it did not create.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一股水流：某物从既有水道被引出，因此它的存在依赖一个并非自己创造的源头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small channel led off from a larger stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：从大河旁引出一条小水道。

branches.en: ORIGINALITY: being led off a stream becomes a judgement when the new channel has no spring of its own.
branches.cn: 原创性：当新水道没有自己的泉眼时，“从别处引水”就变成一种评判。

branches.en: VALUE AND COPYRIGHT: a derivative contract and a derivative work both draw their worth or substance from an underlying original.
branches.cn: 价值与版权：衍生合约与演绎作品都从标的原作取得价值或实质内容。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE AND PROCESS: chemical derivatives and research spin-offs are branches grown from a parent material or project.
branches.cn: 物质与过程：化学衍生物与研究副产品，都是从母体材料或项目长出的分支。

branches.en: WORDS AND NUMBERS: a derived word and a mathematical derivative are both values obtained by a defined operation on a base.
branches.cn: 词与数：派生词与数学导数，都是对基体施加既定运算后得到的值。

branches.en: THE BASE SENSE: every other sense specifies the kind of source and the kind of channel involved.
branches.cn: 基础义：其余义项都只是说明源头与分支的类型。

intro.en: Derivative is derivat- plus -ive. Latin de- and rivus are fused inside the stem; English productively adds -ive, -ation, -ational and -able to build the family.
intro.cn: derivative 是 derivat- 加 -ive。拉丁 de- 与 rivus 已融合在词干内；英语能产地加 -ive、-ation、-ational、-able 来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin rivus 'stream' yields rivulus 'little stream', derivare 'lead off water', and rivalis 'sharing a stream'. English relatives include river, rival, derive and derivation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rivus“溪流”派生 rivulus“小溪”、derivare“引水”、rivalis“共用溪流者”。英语同族词包括 river、rival、derive、derivation。

items.meaning: to obtain from a source; to originate
items.meaningCN: 获得；源自；推导（de-“从”+ rivare“引水”）
items.example: The word derives from an old French term for a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个词源自一个表示边界的古法语词。

items.meaning: the process of deriving; word origin
items.meaningCN: 推导；派生；词源（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The dictionary gives the derivation of the name.
items.exampleCN: 词典给出了这个名字的词源。

items.meaningCN: 派生的；衍生物（-ive 构成形容词与名词）
items.example: The derivative product sold better than the original.
items.exampleCN: 衍生产品比原产品卖得更好。

items.meaning: relating to derivation or word formation
items.meaningCN: 派生的；构词的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The suffix is derivational, not inflectional.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀是派生性的，不是屈折性的。

items.meaning: in a derived or secondary way
items.meaningCN: 派生地；间接地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The right is held derivatively, through the parent company.
items.exampleCN: 这项权利是通过母公司间接持有的。

items.meaningCN: 可推导的；可获得的（-able“能够被……”）
items.example: The result is derivable from two simple assumptions.
items.exampleCN: 这个结果可以从两个简单假设推导出来。

items.meaning: a large natural stream of water
items.meaningCN: 河流（同源词，rivus 的英语形态）
items.example: The river carries sediment to the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这条河把泥沙带向大海。

items.meaningCN: 竞争对手（同源词，原指共用一条溪流的人）
items.example: The two firms became rivals for the same contract.
items.exampleCN: 两家公司成了同一合同的竞争对手。

latinEntries.meaning: to lead water off; to derive
of the same stream; a rival

definition_zh: n. 生物识别技术（指纹、人脸等身份核验）；生物统计学
definition_en: methods of identifying people by measurable body features; also the statistical study of living things
core_image: 一只手指按在玻璃板上，屏幕立刻勾出指纹的纹路
scene: 机场现在用生物识别技术核对旅客与护照。 The airport now uses biometrics to match travellers with their passports.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：biometrics 指以身体特征核验身份的技术；句意是机场用生物识别核对旅客与护照。

pos.zh: 生物识别技术；生物统计学

collocations.zh: 对生物识别的隐私担忧

forms.label: 不可数名词（作技术、学科名）

senses.title: Identity checked by body features
senses.definition: technology that identifies a person from a fingerprint, iris, face or voice
senses.definitionCN: 用指纹、虹膜、面部或声音辨认身份的技术
senses.example: The phone unlocks with biometrics rather than a password.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手机用生物识别解锁，而不是密码。
senses.why: Metron means measure, so biometrics is the measuring of life for identification.
senses.whyCN: metron 意为测量，biometrics 就是为识别而对生命特征进行的测量。

senses.title: Statistics applied to living things
senses.definition: the branch of statistics that deals with measurements taken from living organisms
senses.definitionCN: 处理生物测量数据的统计学分支
senses.example: Biometrics helped the team separate natural variation from real change.
senses.exampleCN: 生物统计帮助团队把自然波动与真实变化区分开。
senses.why: The plural -ics names a field of study, as in physics and economics.
senses.whyCN: 复数词尾 -ics 表示一门学科，如 physics 与 economics。

intro.en: Biometrics joins Greek bios, life, to metron, measure, with the field-forming ending -ics.
intro.cn: biometrics 把希腊语 bios（生命）与 metron（尺度）连接，再加表示学科的 -ics。

items.en: Bios means life, the first element in biology and biometrics.
items.cn: bios 意为生命，是 biology 与 biometrics 的第一构件。

items.en: Metron means measure, the root of metre and symmetry.
items.cn: metron 意为尺度，是 metre 与 symmetry 的词根。

items.en: Biometry first names the statistical study of living things.
items.cn: biometry 最初指对生物的统计研究。

items.en: Fingerprint and voice matching give the word a security sense.
items.cn: 指纹与声纹比对赋予该词安全领域的含义。

items.en: Consumer devices begin to carry biometric sensors.
items.cn: 消费设备开始搭载生物识别传感器。

items.en: Biometrics now usually means identity checks, not statistics.
items.cn: 现代 biometrics 多指身份核验，而非统计学。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bio- or -metr- build; the near-meaning group gathers the security words that surround identity checks.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bio- 或 -metr- 构造；近义组汇集围绕身份核验的安全词汇。

entries.definition: Relating to body measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体测量有关的。

entries.definition: The statistical study of living things.
entries.definitionCN: 对生物的统计研究。

entries.definition: Systems or sets of measurements.
entries.definitionCN: 指标体系。

entries.definition: Relating to biology and medicine together.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物医学有关的。

entries.definition: Recording fingerprints to identify people.
entries.definitionCN: 采集指纹以辨认身份。

entries.definition: The act of proving who someone is.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某人身份的行为。

entries.definition: The process of verifying a claimed identity.
entries.definitionCN: 核实所声称身份的过程。

entries.definition: Close watching of people or places.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或场所的密切监视。

normalIntro.en: Bios is life and metron is measure, so biometrics measures a living body to say who it is.
normalIntro.cn: bios 是生命，metron 是尺度，biometrics 就是测量活体以判定身份。

normal.en: Metric means measure, as in metric system.
normal.cn: metric 意为测量，如公制 metric system。

normal.en: Bio- means life, so biometric is life measurement.
normal.cn: bio- 意为生命，biometric 就是生命测量。

normal.en: The -ics ending marks a field, like physics.
normal.cn: -ics 词尾表示学科，如 physics。

normal.en: Your fingerprint is a measurement you cannot change.
normal.cn: 指纹是一种你改不掉的测量值。

normal.en: Face, iris, voice, gait: four ways to be measured.
normal.cn: 脸、虹膜、声音、步态：四种被测量的方式。

abstract.en: A body used as a password.
abstract.cn: 被当作密码使用的身体。

abstract.en: Measurement that answers only who.
abstract.cn: 只回答「是谁」的测量。

abstract.en: A key you cannot leave at home.
abstract.cn: 无法忘在家里的钥匙。

examples.en: Banks are adding biometrics to phone banking.
examples.cn: 银行正在给手机银行加入生物识别。

examples.en: Critics warn that biometrics cannot be reset like a password.
examples.cn: 批评者提醒说，生物识别不像密码那样可以重置。

examples.en: Her background is in biometrics rather than security.
examples.cn: 她的背景是生物统计，而不是安全技术。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio（生命）+ metrics（测量）——量一量这具身体，就能认出他是谁，这就是生物识别。

root: 希腊 bios（生命）+ metron（尺度）+ -ics（学科、技术）

sensesIntro.en: One word carries two eras: the statistician measuring populations and the gate that measures your face.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词背着两个时代：测量群体的统计学家，以及测量你面部的大门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip on glass while a screen traces the whorls of a print
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖按在玻璃上，屏幕勾出指纹的纹路

branches.en: A thumb pressed on a sensor.
branches.cn: 按在传感器上的拇指。

branches.en: A camera measuring the distance between eyes.
branches.cn: 测量两眼间距的摄像头。

branches.en: A table of growth data from a field study.
branches.cn: 野外研究的长势数据表。

branches.en: A curve drawn from thousands of samples.
branches.cn: 由数千样本画出的曲线。

branches.en: Numbers taken from living bodies.
branches.cn: 从活体上取得的数字。

intro.en: Biometrics is a Greek life-word on a Greek measure-word; the endings below form the vocabulary of measurement.
intro.cn: biometrics 是一个希腊「生命」词加希腊「尺度」词；下面的词缀构成测量词汇。

latinIntro.en: Greek metron is a measure, metria is measurement, and bios is life.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 metron 意为尺度，metria 意为测量，bios 意为生命。

latinEntries.exampleCN: metron 产生 metre 与 symmetry。
bios 产生 biology 与 biometrics。
metria 产生 geometry 与 biometry。

definition_zh: 方差；差异；不一致；变动；变通许可
definition_en: the state of differing or changing, or the statistical measure of how far values spread from their mean
core_image: 一排刻度各自偏离中心线，偏离越远越散，幅度越大
scene: 审计员比对两套账目，发现同一笔支出被记成了两个不同的数。 The two auditors could not explain the variance between the accounts.
sceneCN: 这里指「两套记录之间的不一致」（第 3 个义项：不一致、不符）；句意为两位审计员无法解释两套账目之间的不符。可辨识物件：账本、两列数字、红笔、计算器。

pos.zh: 方差；差异；不一致；变动；变通许可

senses.title: The statistical measure of spread
senses.definition: the average of the squared distances of values from their mean
senses.definitionCN: 各个数值与平均值之差的平方的平均值
senses.example: A large variance means the readings are widely scattered.
senses.exampleCN: 方差大说明各读数分散得很开。
senses.why: The word names the state of differing, and statistics turns that state into one number.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名「不一样」的状态，统计学把这种状态化成一个数。

senses.title: A difference in amount or level
senses.definition: a difference between two amounts, levels or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 两个数量、水平或状况之间的不同
senses.example: A small variance in temperature is normal in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 春天温度有些小波动是正常的。
senses.why: The noun is built on the verb 'to vary', so any departure from a standard is a variance.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由「变化」动词构成，凡偏离标准的都算一种差异。

senses.title: A failure to agree
senses.definition: a disagreement between two records, accounts or statements
senses.definitionCN: 两份记录、账目或说法之间的不符
senses.example: The auditors could not explain the variance between the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 审计员无法解释两套账目之间的不符。
senses.why: Two records that vary from each other leave a discrepancy, and the noun covers that gap too.
senses.whyCN: 两份互不相同的记录留下不符，这个名词也覆盖那道缝。

senses.title: Change from one state to another
senses.definition: the fact of changing or fluctuating over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间变化或起伏的事实
senses.example: Variances in demand make staffing difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 需求的波动使排班变得困难。
senses.why: Varying is an activity, and the noun names its occurrence, especially when it repeats.
senses.whyCN: 「变化」是一个活动，名词命名它的发生，尤其指反复发生。

senses.title: Permission to depart from a rule
senses.definition: official permission to differ from a zoning or building rule
senses.definitionCN: 获准不遵守某条规划或建筑规则的正式许可
senses.example: The owner applied for a variance to build closer to the road.
senses.exampleCN: 业主申请变通许可，以便把房子建得离路更近。
senses.why: Law borrows the word because the applicant asks to vary from the rule without breaking it.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用这个词，因为申请人请求在不违规的前提下偏离规则。

senses.title: The gap between budget and actual
senses.titleCN: 预算与实际之间的差异
senses.definition: the difference between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded
senses.definitionCN: 计划数字与实际记录数字之间的差
senses.example: A favourable budget variance appeared in the third quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 第三季度出现了有利的预算差异。
senses.why: Accounting gives every departure from plan a line, and calls that line a variance.
senses.whyCN: 会计给每一处偏离计划的地方列一行，并称这一行为差异。

senses.title: The sample variance
senses.definition: the statistic computed from a sample, usually with a divisor one less than the count
senses.definitionCN: 由样本算出的统计量，除数通常比个数少一
senses.example: The sample variance slightly overstates the spread of small samples.
senses.exampleCN: 样本方差会略微高估小样本的离散程度。
senses.why: Sample and population versions differ only in the divisor, so one word covers both with a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 样本与总体两个版本只差除数，因此一个词加个限定语就能覆盖两者。

senses.title: The degree of departure from the norm
senses.definition: the extent to which something departs from what is usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 某事物偏离通常或预期状态的程度
senses.example: Any variance from the usual pattern was noted in the log.
senses.exampleCN: 凡偏离常规模式之处都记进了日志。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps only the idea of departure, with no numbers and no rule attached.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留「偏离」这个观念，既不附数字，也不附规则。

intro.en: Variance comes through Old French from Latin variantia, a noun from variare 'to change', itself from varius 'diverse, mottled'. The origin of varius is not fully settled.
intro.cn: variance 经古法语来自拉丁 variantia，出自动词 variare「变化」，再上溯形容词 varius「多样的、斑驳的」；varius 的更早来源尚无定论。

items.en: Varius meant 'diverse, varied, mottled'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; connections proposed to other roots are hypotheses, not demonstrated links.
items.cn: varius 意为「多样的、变化的、斑驳的」。其更早来源不确定；与别的词根的联系只是假说，未获证明。

items.en: Variare 'to change, vary' turned the adjective into a verb of altering.
items.cn: variare「改变、使变化」把形容词变成表示改变的动作词。

items.en: Variantia named the state of being varied, hence a difference or a divergence.
items.cn: variantia 指「有变化」的状态，因此指差异或背离。

items.en: Old French variance carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as the state of disagreeing.
items.cn: 古法语 variance 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指意见不合的状态。

items.en: The technical sense of squared spread belongs to nineteenth-century statistics and was standardised in the twentieth.
items.cn: 「平方离散」的技术义属十九世纪统计学，到二十世纪才标准化。

items.en: The permission sense and the budget sense are specialised offshoots; neither has a firmly dated first citation.
items.cn: 许可义与预算义都是专门化的分支，两者的确切首见书证都无定论。

note.en: Group one holds formations from the same varying root that are constantly swapped; group two holds words for a departure or a disagreement.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「变化」词根、常被混用的构词；第二组是表示「偏离」或「不一致」的词。

entries.definition: A single differing form or version, not the state of differing.
entries.definitionCN: 一个具体的不同形式或版本，而非「不一样」的状态。

entries.definition: The process or extent of change, often deliberate or gradual.
entries.definitionCN: 变化的过程或幅度，常指有意的或渐进的改变。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning several different kinds, with no measurement implied.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指若干不同种类，不含度量之意。

entries.definition: The quality of having many different kinds, used of goods, species or experience.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有许多不同种类的性质，用于商品、物种或体验。

entries.definition: A departure from a standard or a course, usually measured against a norm.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离标准或航道的程度，通常对照某个规范来量。

entries.definition: A mismatch between two things that ought to agree, such as accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 本应一致的两者之间的不符，如账目。

entries.definition: Repeated up-and-down movement in a level or price.
entries.definitionCN: 水平或价格的反复升降。

entries.definition: The general word for two things not being the same.
entries.definitionCN: 表示两事物不一样的通称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'varied, mottled', so the noun names the state of not being uniform.
normal.cn: 词根意为「多样的、斑驳的」，因此这个名词指「不齐一」的状态。

normal.en: One family runs vary, variant, variation, variable, variability and variance.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：变化、变体、变化、变量、变异性、方差。

normal.en: Statistics uses the squared distances from the mean; the plain word uses any departure at all.
normal.cn: 统计学用与平均值之差的平方；日常用法则指任何偏离。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the specialised uses: at variance with, budget variance, zoning variance.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出专门用法：与某物不一致、预算差异、规划变通许可。

normal.en: Two records that will not agree are 'at variance', which is the same idea as two numbers that scatter.
normal.cn: 两份对不上的记录叫「不一致」，这与两个散开的数字是同一想法。

abstract.en: Picture a row of marks drifting away from a centre line, some far, some near.
abstract.cn: 想象一排记号偏离中心线，有的远，有的近。

abstract.en: Picture two ledger books open side by side with one figure circled in each, and the circles not matching.
abstract.cn: 想象两本账册并排摊开，每本上圈着一个数字，两个圈却对不上。

abstract.en: Picture a road where one house is allowed to stand a little closer to the kerb than the rule says.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路上有一户获准比规定稍微靠近路缘建房。

examples.en: The variance of the sample was larger than expected.
examples.cn: 这个样本的方差比预期大。

examples.en: Her account is at variance with the official record.
examples.cn: 她的说法与官方记录不一致。

examples.en: The council granted a variance for the taller sign.
examples.cn: 议会批准了这块更高招牌的变通许可。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「多样的、斑驳的」，动词意为「变化」，加名词词尾就成「不一样的状态」；统计学把这种散开化成一个数，法律则把偏离规则的特许也叫这个名字。

root: 拉丁 variantia「差异」＝ variare「变化」＋名词词尾，variare 出自动词化之前的形容词 varius「多样的、斑驳的」；varius 更早来源不确定。英语经古法语传入。同族 vary、variant、variation、variable 只差词尾。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one state: things that were expected to be alike are not. That state is then counted as squared spread, seen as a fluctuation, booked as a ledger gap, licensed by law, and finally named as any departure from the norm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种状态展开：本应一样的东西并不一样。这种状态再依次被算成平方离散、看成波动、记成账目差额、由法律特许，最后被命名为任何偏离常规的程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: marks on a rule drifting away from the centre line, some far and some near.
core.cn: 核心意象：尺上的记号一个个偏离中心线，有的远有的近。

branches.en: MEASURE: the statistical sense turns unlikeness into one squared number, with sample and population versions.
branches.cn: 度量：统计义把「不一样」化成一个平方数，并分样本与总体两个版本。

branches.en: DRIFT: a difference in level and a fluctuation over time are the same departure, seen once and seen repeatedly.
branches.cn: 漂移：水平上的差异与时间上的波动，是同一种偏离的一次看法与反复看法。

branches.en: RECORDS: two sets of figures that will not agree, whether in an audit or a budget.
branches.cn: 记录：两套对不上的数字，无论在审计里还是在预算里。

branches.en: LICENCE: law lets an applicant differ from a rule without breaking it.
branches.cn: 特许：法律允许申请人偏离规则而不违规。

branches.en: THE NORM: with numbers gone, variance is simply distance from what is usual.
branches.cn: 常规：数字去掉之后，方差就是与通常状态的距离。

intro.en: Variance is a Latin abstract noun built on a verb of changing, and the whole family turns up in English with different endings.
intro.cn: variance 是一个拉丁抽象名词，建立在表示变化的动词上；整个词族以不同词尾出现在英语中。

latinIntro.en: Latin varius and variare give variance, variant, variation and variable; the ending -antia becomes English -ance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 varius 与 variare 衍生 variance、variant、variation、variable；词尾 -antia 在英语中变为 -ance。

definition_zh: 近似；接近；近似值；粗略估算；逼近；近似物
definition_en: the act of coming close to something; a value, estimate, or model that is close to the true one but not exact; also a thing that resembles another
core_image: 一支箭落在靶心旁边：没有正中，但已经足够靠近
scene: 一支箭射中靶心旁一指宽处，教练用小尺量出偏差，记录在计分板上。 The coach called the measured distance an approximation, not an exact value.
sceneCN: 这里 approximation 是「近似、接近」（第 1 个义项：靠近某物或某个值的行为）；句意：教练说这段距离只是近似值，不是精确测量。图中可辨识物件：弓、箭、靶心、小尺、记分板。

pos.zh: 近似；接近；近似值；粗略估算；逼近

derivatives.zh: 近似的；大约的；接近；近似

senses.title: Coming near: the act of approaching
senses.definition: the act of coming near or close to a place, thing, or value
senses.definitionCN: 靠近某个地点、事物或数值的行为
senses.example: The approximation of the storm forced the boats back to harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴的逼近迫使船只返回港口。
senses.why: Latin approximare is ad- 'to' plus proximare 'come near', from proximus 'nearest'. The earliest English sense, recorded in the early 15th c., is simply the act of coming close.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 approximare 是 ad-“向”加 proximare“靠近”，后者出自 proximus“最近的”。英语最早的义项记录于 15 世纪早期，就是“靠近”这个动作。

senses.title: A value close to the truth: the near figure
senses.definition: a number, measurement, or result that is close to the true value but not exact
senses.definitionCN: 接近真实值但不精确的数字、测量或结果
senses.example: Pi to two decimals is the approximation 3.14.
senses.exampleCN: 圆周率保留两位小数，近似值是 3.14。
senses.why: From the act of coming near, the noun shifts to the result of that approach: a figure that has come close to the true value. The 1650s sense 'result of approximating' is exactly this landing point.
senses.whyCN: 名词从“靠近的动作”转到“靠近的结果”：一个已经接近真值的数字。17 世纪 50 年代出现的“近似的结果”义，正是这个落点。

senses.title: A rough estimate: close enough for the purpose
senses.definition: a rough calculation or estimate that is accepted because it is close enough for a practical purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为实际目的而接受的粗略计算或估计，因为已经足够接近
senses.example: A quick approximation put the crowd at three thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 快速估算一下，人群大约有三千人。
senses.why: The approach is deliberately not exact: you stop when you are near enough. Approximation here names the stopping point, not a failure to reach the target.
senses.whyCN: 这种靠近是刻意不精确的：够近就停下。这里的 approximation 命名的是这个停下的位置，而不是“没打中靶心”的失败。

senses.title: A near copy: something resembling another
senses.titleCN: 近似仿本：像，但不是原物
senses.definition: a thing that resembles another thing in appearance or character without being the same
senses.definitionCN: 在外观或性质上像另一物、但并不相同的东西
senses.example: The model is only an approximation of the real bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型只是真实桥梁的一个近似物。
senses.why: Two objects can come near each other in shape. The copy approaches the original without touching it, so approximation becomes resemblance rather than measurement.
senses.whyCN: 两个物件可以在形状上彼此靠近。仿本接近原作却没有重合，因此 approximation 从测量变成“相似之物”。

senses.title: Mathematical approximation: a curve that comes close
senses.titleCN: 数学逼近：曲线靠上目标
senses.definition: a mathematical expression or method that comes close to a value, curve, or function without equalling it
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个值、曲线或函数但不与之相等的数学表达式或方法
senses.example: The students used a straight line as an approximation to the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们用一条直线作为这条曲线的近似。
senses.why: Here the approach is formalised: a simpler object is chosen because it comes near the true one. Approximation becomes a tool for replacing the hard exact object with a near one.
senses.whyCN: 这里的靠近被形式化了：选择一个更简单的对象，因为它接近真实对象。approximation 于是成为“用近似的对象替换难处理的精确对象”的工具。

senses.title: Numerical or statistical approximation: close by method
senses.titleCN: 数值或统计近似：用方法靠近
senses.definition: a result obtained by a numerical or statistical method that converges on, or estimates, a true value
senses.definitionCN: 通过数值或统计方法得到的、收敛到或估计出真值的结果
senses.example: The simulation's approximation improved with every extra round of sampling.
senses.exampleCN: 每增加一轮抽样，模拟的近似就更精确。
senses.why: The approach is now repeated by a procedure: each step brings the result nearer. Approximation names both the method's output and the closeness it achieves.
senses.whyCN: 这里的靠近由一套程序反复执行：每一步都把结果带得更近。approximation 既命名方法的输出，也命名它达到的接近程度。

senses.title: Approximation to a standard: nearing the target
senses.definition: a state of coming close to a standard, norm, or desired level without fully reaching it
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个标准、规范或理想水平但尚未完全达到的状态
senses.example: The new engine's efficiency is a close approximation to the design target.
senses.exampleCN: 新发动机的效率已很接近设计目标。
senses.why: What is approached is now an abstract target. The word measures the gap that remains, so it can describe progress toward a norm rather than a number.
senses.whyCN: 此时被靠近的是一个抽象目标。这个词衡量仍然存在的差距，因此可以描述朝某个规范取得的进展，而不只是一个数字。

senses.title: A model close to reality: useful but not exact
senses.titleCN: 接近现实的模型：有用但不精确
senses.definition: a simplified model or description that is close enough to reality to be useful, while knowingly not exact
senses.definitionCN: 一种简化模型或描述，接近现实到足以有用，同时明知并不精确
senses.example: The economic model is an approximation that ignores migration.
senses.exampleCN: 这个经济模型是一个忽略了人口迁移的近似。
senses.why: A model approaches the world but never becomes the world. Approximation here names the accepted distance between a simplified account and the reality it describes.
senses.whyCN: 模型靠近世界，却永远不会变成世界。这里的 approximation 命名的是简化描述与被描述现实之间被接受的距离。

senses.title: The quality of being near but not identical
senses.definition: the quality or state of being close to something in value, form, or meaning without being identical to it
senses.definitionCN: 在数值、形式或意义上接近某物、但不完全相同的性质或状态
senses.example: The translation's approximation to the original is its greatest strength and its limit.
senses.exampleCN: 这份译文与原作的近似，既是它最大的优点，也是它的局限。
senses.why: The noun moves from countable results to an abstract quality: the degree of nearness itself. This is the latest and most general branch, where approximation means 'closeness without identity'.
senses.whyCN: 名词从可数的结果转到抽象性质：接近的程度本身。这是最晚、也最一般化的分支，approximation 在此意为“接近但不重合”。

intro.en: Approximation is an action noun in -ion, from Latin -ionem, naming an act or its result. It comes from Latin approximare 'come near to' — ad- 'to' plus proximare 'come near' — or from the English verb approximate. The root proximus is the superlative of prope 'near', so the whole word is built from nearness, not from price or ownership.
intro.cn: approximation 是带 -ion 的动作名词，-ion 来自拉丁语 -ionem，命名动作或其结果。它来自拉丁语 approximare“接近”——ad-“向”加 proximare“靠近”——或来自英语动词 approximate。词根 proximus 是 prope“近”的最高级，因此整个词建立在“近”上，而不是“价格”或“所有权”。

items.en: First recorded as approximacioun, 'act of coming near or close'. The earliest sense is physical or spatial approach, not numerical accuracy.
items.cn: 最早记录为 approximacioun，意为“靠近、接近的动作”。最早的义项是物理或空间上的接近，不是数值精度。

items.en: The noun is the action noun of approximate (v.), or is taken directly from Latin approximare. The suffix -ion marks the action or its result: the coming near, then the thing that has come near.
items.cn: 这个名词是动词 approximate 的动作名词，或直接取自拉丁语 approximare。后缀 -ion 标记动作或其结果：先是“靠近”，再是“已经靠近的东西”。

items.en: Approximare 'come near to' = ad- 'to' + proximare 'come near'. The prefix points the movement toward a target, so the verb means approach rather than mere proximity.
items.cn: approximare“接近”= ad-“向”+ proximare“靠近”。前缀把运动指向一个目标，因此这个动词是“朝……靠近”，而不只是“在旁边”。

items.en: Proximare comes from proximus 'nearest', the superlative of prope 'near'. The root is a ranking of nearness, which is why an approximation is the closest available figure rather than an exact one.
items.cn: proximare 来自 proximus“最近的”，即 prope“近”的最高级。这个词根是对“近”的排序，因此 approximation 是“可得到的最接近的数字”，而不是精确值。

items.en: The adjective approximate is recorded in the 1640s meaning 'near in position, close to', and the noun's sense 'result of approximating' in the 1650s.
items.cn: 形容词 approximate 记录于 17 世纪 40 年代，义为“位置上靠近的”；名词“近似的结果”义记录于 17 世纪 50 年代。

items.en: The sense 'near in accuracy or correctness' appears in 1816. This is the branch behind approximations to a true value, a standard, or a model of reality.
items.cn: “在准确度或正确性上接近”的义项出现于 1816 年。这就是“接近真值、标准或现实模型”的分支。

note.en: The first group puts approximation beside its own base and the two look-alike roots that must not be confused with it; the second group separates it from estimate, estimation and resemblance.
note.cn: 第一组把 approximation 放在它自己的基础词，以及两个绝不能与它混淆的形近词根旁边；第二组把它与 estimate、estimation、resemblance 分开。

entries.definition: close to the true value or position but not exact. It is the adjective and verb behind approximation, built on the same proximus root.
entries.definitionCN: 接近真实值或位置但不精确的。它是 approximation 背后的形容词与动词，建立在同一 proximus 词根上。

entries.definition: suitable or proper for a purpose. It comes from proprius 'one's own', not from proximus 'nearest', despite the similar opening.
entries.definitionCN: 适合某目的的；恰当的。它来自 proprius“自己的”，而不是 proximus“最近的”，尽管开头很像。

entries.definition: to value, be grateful for, or rise in value. It comes from pretium 'price', a third root that merely looks like the other two.
entries.definitionCN: 重视；感激；增值。它来自 pretium“价格”，是第三个只是看起来相似的词根。

entries.definition: a judgment of size, value, or amount based on evidence. An estimate need not be close to a known true value, while an approximation always suggests closeness.
entries.definitionCN: 依据证据对大小、价值或数量作出的判断。estimate 不一定接近已知真值，而 approximation 总含有“已经靠近”的意思。

entries.definition: the act of estimating, or a considered opinion of worth. It stresses judgment, while approximation stresses nearness to an exact value.
entries.definitionCN: 估算的行为，或经过考虑的价值判断。它强调判断，而 approximation 强调与精确值的接近。

entries.definition: the state of looking like someone or something else. It covers the 'near copy' branch, while approximation can also be numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像某人某物的状态。它覆盖“近似仿本”这一分支，而 approximation 还可以是数值上的。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: proximus 'nearest' and prope 'near', the ad- prefix, the -ion action noun, and the fixed phrases rough approximation and successive approximation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：proximus“最近的”与 prope“近”、ad- 前缀、-ion 动作名词，以及 rough approximation、successive approximation 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Prope is 'near' and proximus is 'nearest': approximation is the figure that has come nearest to the true one.
normal.cn: prope 是“近”，proximus 是“最近的”：approximation 就是已经最靠近真值的那个数字。

normal.en: Ad- means 'to': approximare is to move toward a target, so every approximation contains a direction of approach.
normal.cn: ad- 意为“向”：approximare 就是朝目标移动，因此每个 approximation 里都含有一个靠近的方向。

normal.en: Approximate is the adjective and verb; approximately is the adverb; approximation is the noun of the act or result.
normal.cn: approximate 是形容词和动词，approximately 是副词，approximation 是动作或结果的名词。

normal.en: A rough approximation and a first approximation are standard phrases: close enough to start, not close enough to finish.
normal.cn: a rough approximation 与 a first approximation 是标准说法：近到可以开始，但还没近到可以结束。

normal.en: Successive approximation is a real method: each attempt comes closer than the one before.
normal.cn: successive approximation 是一种真实的方法：每一次尝试都比上一次更靠近。

abstract.en: An arrow lands beside the bullseye: the score depends on how near, and the nearness is the whole point.
abstract.cn: 一支箭落在靶心旁边：得分取决于有多近，而“近”正是全部意义。

abstract.en: A staircase tries to follow a smooth curve: each step is flat and exact, yet the staircase only approximates the curve.
abstract.cn: 一段楼梯试图跟随一条光滑曲线：每级台阶都是平直而精确的，但整段楼梯只是曲线的近似。

abstract.en: A pencil sketch of a face: fewer lines than a photograph, yet near enough for you to recognise who it is.
abstract.cn: 一张人脸的铅笔速写：线条比照片少得多，却已经近到让你认得出那是谁。

examples.en: The figure is an approximation; the exact cost will be known after the survey.
examples.cn: 这个数字只是近似值；确切成本要等勘测之后才知道。

examples.en: Her description was a fair approximation of what we saw.
examples.cn: 她的描述相当接近我们所看到的情形。

examples.en: The method uses successive approximation to solve the equation.
examples.cn: 这种方法用逐次逼近来解方程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普若克西美申」——阿普若（Ap-pro）射出一箭，克西（Ke Xi）喊“差一点”，美申（Mei Shen）把箭拔下来又朝靶心靠近一步 → approximation 近似、接近

root: 源自拉丁语 approximare“接近”（ad-“向”+ proximare“靠近”，proximus“最近的”是 prope“近”的最高级），核心是“靠近”，再由空间接近引申为数值与判断上的近似。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of approximation all follow one movement: something comes near a target without landing on it. From physical approach and a near figure, the word extends to rough estimates, near copies, mathematical and numerical methods, standards, models, and finally the abstract quality of closeness.
sensesIntro.cn: approximation 的九个义项都遵循同一个动作：某物朝目标靠近，却没有落在目标上。从物理接近与一个接近的数字，它扩展到粗略估算、近似仿本、数学与数值方法、标准、模型，最后到抽象的“接近性”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow landing beside the bullseye, close but not exact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭落在靶心旁边，很近，但不正中。

branches.en: APPROACH AND RESULT: the act of coming near, and the near figure that results.
branches.cn: 靠近与结果：接近的动作，以及由此得到的接近数字。

branches.en: ROUGH ESTIMATE: closeness accepted because it is enough for the purpose.
branches.cn: 粗略估算：因为够用而被接受的接近。

branches.en: NEAR COPY: resemblance, where one object comes near another in form.
branches.cn: 近似仿本：相似，一个物件在形态上靠近另一个。

branches.en: FORMAL METHODS: curves, functions and procedures that converge on a true value.
branches.cn: 形式方法：曲线、函数与程序朝真值收敛。

branches.en: STANDARDS, MODELS AND QUALITY: nearing a target, modelling reality, and closeness as such.
branches.cn: 标准、模型与性质：靠近目标、模拟现实，以及“接近”本身。

intro.en: Approximation is approximat- plus -ion, from Latin -ionem, an action-or-result noun. The same stem gives approximate, approximately, approximative, approximator and approximated; the bare proxim- root lives on in proximity and proximate.
intro.cn: approximation 是 approximat- 加 -ion，后者来自拉丁语 -ionem，构成动作或结果名词。同一词干给出 approximate、approximately、approximative、approximator 与 approximated；光秃的 proxim- 词根仍活在 proximity 与 proximate 中。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin approximare, ad- plus proximare 'come near'. Proximare comes from proximus 'nearest', the superlative of prope 'near'; English proximity keeps the same proximus stem.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 approximare，即 ad- 加 proximare“靠近”。proximare 来自 proximus“最近的”，即 prope“近”的最高级；英语 proximity 保留同一 proximus 词干。

items.meaning: the act of coming near, or a near value or model
items.meaningCN: 近似；接近；近似值（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The map is only an approximation of the coast.
items.exampleCN: 这幅地图只是海岸线的一个近似。

items.meaning: to come near, or close to the true value
items.meaningCN: 接近；近似的（-ate 构成动词或形容词）
items.example: The repair will approximate two hundred dollars.
items.exampleCN: 维修费大约要两百美元。

items.meaningCN: 大约；近似地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The trip takes approximately three hours.
items.exampleCN: 这段行程大约需要三小时。

items.meaning: of the nature of an approximation; not exact
items.meaningCN: 近似的；接近的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The study offers only an approximative answer.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究只给出一个近似的答案。

items.meaning: a person or device that produces approximations
items.meaningCN: 近似者；近似计算装置（-or 表示做该动作的人或物）
items.example: The software acts as a curve approximator.
items.exampleCN: 这个软件起到曲线逼近器的作用。

items.meaning: estimated or brought close to a value
items.meaningCN: 被近似的；估算出的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The approximated cost was still too high.
items.exampleCN: 估算出的成本仍然太高。

items.meaningCN: 接近；邻近（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The house's proximity to the river worried the owners.
items.exampleCN: 这房子离河太近，让房主担心。

items.meaning: nearest in space, time, or cause
items.meaningCN: 最近的；直接的（-ate 构成形容词）
items.example: The proximate cause of the fire was a faulty wire.
items.exampleCN: 火灾的直接原因是一根故障电线。

items.meaning: able to be approximated or estimated closely
items.meaningCN: 可逼近的；可近似估算的（-able 表示能够被……的）
items.example: The function is approximable by a short series.
items.exampleCN: 这个函数可以用一个短级数逼近。

definition_zh: 轨道的；在轨的；眼窝的；原子轨道、分子轨道（名词）
definition_en: relating to an orbit, or (as a noun) a region where an electron is likely to be found
core_image: 一只小金属盒被机械臂夹住，盒面贴着一条绕地球一圈的细线标签
scene: 实验室里一只小金属盒被机械臂夹住，盒面贴着说明它绕地球飞行的标签。 A small metal box carries an orbital label showing its path around the earth.
sceneCN: 这里 orbital 指「在轨运行的」（第 2 个义项：用于在轨设施与轨道碎片等）；句意为小金属盒上贴着一张标出它绕地路径的在轨标签。图中可辨识物件：机械臂、金属盒、标签、绕地细线、实验台。

pos.zh: 轨道的；在轨的；眼窝的
原子轨道；分子轨道（物理化学术语）

senses.title: Relating to an orbit
senses.definition: relating to the path of a body around another
senses.definitionCN: 与一个天体绕另一个天体运行的路径有关的
senses.example: The orbital path of the comet was plotted in red.
senses.exampleCN: 彗星的轨道路径用红色绘出。
senses.why: the word is simply orbit plus the adjective suffix -al, so its base sense is 'of the track'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 orbit 加形容词后缀 -al，因此基本义为「轨迹的」。

senses.title: Operating in orbit
senses.definition: used of objects, stations or debris that are actually circling the earth or another body
senses.definitionCN: 指真正绕地球或其他天体运行的物体、设施或碎片
senses.example: A small metal box carries an orbital label showing its path around the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 小金属盒上贴着一张标出它绕地路径的在轨标签。
senses.why: engineers needed a short adjective for 'in orbit', and orbital filled the gap without a phrase like 'in orbit'.
senses.whyCN: 工程师需要一个简短形容词表示「在轨」，orbital 正好填空，不必说「in orbit」。

senses.title: The atomic orbital
senses.definition: a region around a nucleus where an electron is most likely to be found
senses.definitionCN: 原子核周围电子最可能出现的区域
senses.example: Each electron occupies an orbital with a fixed energy.
senses.exampleCN: 每个电子占据一个能量确定的轨道。
senses.why: quantum mechanics replaced circling paths with probability clouds, but kept the old word by turning it into a noun.
senses.whyCN: 量子力学用概率云取代了绕行路径，却把这个旧词转为名词保留下来。

senses.title: The molecular orbital
senses.definition: a spread of electron probability over a whole molecule rather than one atom
senses.definitionCN: 电子概率分布在整个分子而非单个原子上的区域
senses.example: Bonding electrons fill the lowest molecular orbital first.
senses.exampleCN: 成键电子先填满最低的分子轨道。
senses.why: when atoms join, their orbitals combine, so the same noun was extended from atoms to molecules.
senses.whyCN: 原子结合时其轨道也合并，因此同一个名词从原子扩展到了分子。

senses.title: Of the eye socket
senses.definition: relating to the bony cavity around the eye, as in the orbital bone or orbital floor
senses.definitionCN: 与眼周骨腔有关的，如眶骨或眶底
senses.example: The surgeon repaired the orbital floor after the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤后外科医生修复了眶底。
senses.why: Latin used orbita for the socket too, so the adjective carries both the orbit and the eye socket without conflict.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语也用 orbita 指眼窝，因此这个形容词同时承载轨道与眼窝两义而不冲突。

senses.title: Orbital quantities
senses.titleCN: 轨道物理量：速度、周期、平面
senses.definition: used of measurable properties of motion in an orbit, such as velocity, period and plane
senses.definitionCN: 指轨道运动中的可测属性，如速度、周期与平面
senses.example: Orbital velocity falls as the satellite moves farther out.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星越往外，轨道速度越低。
senses.why: once orbits are treated as curves with numbers, the adjective attaches naturally to every quantity describing them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦轨道被当作带数值的曲线，这个形容词自然就附着于描述它们的每个量。

senses.title: An orbital road
senses.definition: in British English, a road that circles a city instead of passing through it
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中绕城而不穿城的公路
senses.example: Traffic shifted to the orbital motorway within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 不到一年，车流就转到了环城高速上。
senses.why: a ring road does literally go round a centre, so the astronomical picture transferred to traffic planning.
senses.whyCN: 环路确实绕着一个中心走，因此天文学图景被转用到交通规划上。

senses.title: An orbital launch vehicle
senses.titleCN: 具备入轨能力的运载火箭
senses.definition: used of a rocket powerful enough to place a payload into orbit rather than only on a short flight
senses.definitionCN: 指推力足以把载荷送入轨道、而不只是短程飞行的火箭
senses.example: Only an orbital rocket could carry the full laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 只有具备入轨能力的火箭才能运载整个实验室。
senses.why: the adjective distinguishes reaching space from reaching orbit, a distinction engineers care about.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词区分「到达太空」与「到达轨道」，而工程师很在意这一区别。

intro.en: Orbital is orbit plus the Latin adjective suffix -alis, giving English -al. The noun use for electron clouds dates from twentieth-century quantum chemistry. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: orbital 是 orbit 加拉丁形容词后缀 -alis（英语作 -al）。指电子云的名词用法来自 20 世纪量子化学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Orbita 'wheel-rut, track' is the base, and Latin already used it for the eye socket.
items.cn: orbita「车辙、轨迹」是基础，拉丁语已用它指眼窝。

items.en: Anatomical Latin formed orbitalis 'of the socket', which is the model for the English adjective.
items.cn: 解剖学拉丁语构成 orbitalis「眼窝的」，是英语形容词的模板。

items.en: English borrowed Latin adjectives ending in -alis as -al, so orbit produced orbital.
items.cn: 英语把以 -alis 结尾的拉丁形容词借作 -al，于是 orbit 产生 orbital。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective became a noun for an electron's probability region, first for atoms and then for molecules.
items.cn: 20 世纪这个形容词转为名词，指电子的概率区域，先用于原子，再用于分子。

items.en: Space agencies adopted it for anything in orbit: orbital debris, orbital station, orbital launch.
items.cn: 航天机构用它指一切在轨事物：轨道碎片、在轨空间站、入轨发射。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English use of orbital is not firmly dated, and the pre-Latin origin of orbis remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：orbital 最早的英语用例没有可靠年代；orbis 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the orbit family forms that are often confused; group two holds adjectives of shape and position.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的 orbit 词族形式；第二组是形状与位置类形容词。

entries.definition: The path itself or the act of circling; orbital only describes something related to it.
entries.definitionCN: 路径本身或绕行动作；orbital 只描述与之相关的事物。

entries.definition: A spacecraft that orbits; the -er suffix marks the thing doing the circling.
entries.definitionCN: 绕行的航天器；-er 后缀标记执行绕行的物体。

entries.definition: The participle for the ongoing motion, as in an orbiting telescope.
entries.definitionCN: 表示正在进行的运动的分词，如「在轨望远镜」。

entries.definition: The flat surface an orbit lies in; the two-word phrase names a plane rather than a property.
entries.definitionCN: 轨道所在的平面；这个两词短语命名的是平面，而非属性。

entries.definition: Shaped like a circle; an orbit can be circular, but orbital says nothing about shape.
entries.definitionCN: 圆形的；轨道可以是圆的，但 orbital 不涉及形状。

entries.definition: Turning around a centre; it stresses the motion rather than the path's geometry.
entries.definitionCN: 绕中心转动；强调运动而非路径几何。

entries.definition: Situated on an outer boundary; it resembles the 'orbital road' sense but carries no circle.
entries.definitionCN: 位于外缘的；与「环城路」义相近，但不含圆圈意象。

entries.definition: Relating to space in general; orbital is a much narrower, path-specific adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与空间有关；orbital 是窄得多、专指路径的形容词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: orbit + -al: the plain adjective of the track.
normal.cn: orbit + -al：轨迹的普通形容词。

normal.en: Latin orbitalis was first an anatomical word for the eye socket.
normal.cn: 拉丁 orbitalis 最早是解剖学词，指眼窝。

normal.en: The family runs orbit, orbital, orbiter, orbiting, orbitally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 orbit、orbital、orbiter、orbiting、orbitally。

normal.en: Fixed terms: orbital period, orbital velocity, orbital plane, orbital debris.
normal.cn: 固定术语：轨道周期、轨道速度、轨道平面、轨道碎片。

normal.en: In chemistry the noun orbital names an electron's probability cloud.
normal.cn: 化学中名词 orbital 指电子的概率云。

abstract.en: Picture a ring road drawn around a city that refuses to be crossed.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绕着不肯被穿过的城市画出的环路。

abstract.en: Picture a haze that surrounds a lamp without ever touching it.
abstract.cn: 想象一团雾围着灯，却从不碰到它。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a box that says where the box will forever go.
abstract.cn: 想象盒子上贴着标签，写明它将永远走的路。

examples.en: Orbital debris poses a growing risk to working satellites.
examples.cn: 轨道碎片对工作中的卫星构成越来越大的风险。

examples.en: The orbital period of the station is about ninety minutes.
examples.cn: 该空间站的轨道周期约为九十分钟。

examples.en: Chemists draw the shape of each orbital before predicting a bond.
examples.cn: 化学家在预测成键之前先画出每个轨道的形状。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，比特（orbital）」——哦，它每比特都绕着走 → 轨道的

root: orbit（拉丁 orbita「车辙」）+ 拉丁形容词后缀 -alis（英语 -al）；拉丁 orbitalis 本为解剖学「眼窝的」，20 世纪又转为名词指电子概率区域。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the plain adjective, then branch to in-orbit hardware, to electron clouds and molecules, to the eye socket, to measured quantities, to a ring road and to a launch vehicle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从普通形容词开始，再分向在轨硬件、电子云与分子、眼窝、可测物理量、环城公路与运载火箭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line drawn once around a centre, marking everything that stays near it.
core.cn: 核心意象：绕中心画的一道细线，标记一切靠近它的事物。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND PLACE: the adjective describes a path, then things living on it.
branches.cn: 属性与位置：这个形容词先描述路径，再描述在路径上的事物。

branches.en: QUANTUM REUSE: atoms and molecules keep the old word for a new kind of cloud.
branches.cn: 量子复用：原子与分子用旧词指一种新的云。

branches.en: BODY RING: the eye socket was the word's first English home.
branches.cn: 身体之环：眼窝是这个词最早的英语归宿。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: quantities and launch capability make the orbit a specification.
branches.cn: 工程：物理量与入轨能力把轨道变成一项指标。

branches.en: CITY RING: a road repeats the circle at human scale.
branches.cn: 城市之环：一条路在人的尺度上重复了这个圆。

intro.en: Orbital is a Latin noun plus a Latin adjective suffix; the same suffix turns it into technical terms across several fields.
intro.cn: orbital 是一个拉丁名词加拉丁形容词后缀；同一后缀在多个领域把它变成技术术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin orbita 'track' and orbitalis 'of the socket' supply the base; orbis 'circle' supplies the wider family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 orbita「轨迹」与 orbitalis「眼窝的」提供基础；orbis「圆」提供更广的词族。

items.example: The suffix turns orbit into orbital.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 orbit 变成 orbital。

items.example: The atom has three filled orbitals.
items.exampleCN: 该原子有三个填满的轨道。

items.meaning: at the level of an orbit
items.example: The two stars are orbitally locked.
items.exampleCN: 这两颗星在轨道上被锁定。

items.example: The orbiter photographed the ice cap.
items.exampleCN: 轨道飞行器拍下了冰盖。

items.example: The two orbits share one orbital plane.
items.exampleCN: 两条轨道共用一个轨道平面。

items.example: Orbital debris can disable a satellite.
items.exampleCN: 轨道碎片能使卫星失效。

definition_zh: 丑角；滑稽可笑的人；粗俗的逗乐者
definition_en: a ridiculous person who clowns about to amuse others
core_image: 翻着跟头的小丑，动作夸张惹人笑
scene: 宴会上他做鬼脸、学鹅走路，把满座逗得前仰后合。 The guest acted like a buffoon to keep everyone laughing.
sceneCN: 这里 buffoon 是「丑角、滑稽可笑的人」（第 1 个义项：以夸张滑稽举动逗乐）；句意是这位客人扮丑逗众人发笑。

pos.zh: 丑角；小丑；滑稽粗俗的逗乐者

derivatives.zh: 由 buffoon 加 -ery 构成，义为「滑稽表演，丑态」
由 buffoon 加 -ish 构成，义为「小丑般的，滑稽可笑的」
近义词，义为「小丑」，词源不同

senses.title: A comic performer
senses.definition: a performer who amuses by exaggerated gestures, pratfalls and jokes
senses.definitionCN: 以夸张动作、摔跤和笑话逗人发笑的表演者
senses.example: The medieval court kept a buffoon to entertain the king.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪宫廷养着弄臣为国王取乐。
senses.why: The Italian source names a trotting dance; a prancing figure became the comic type.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语源词指一种蹦跳的舞，蹦蹦跳跳的身影遂定型为滑稽角色。

senses.title: A ridiculous person
senses.definition: a person whose behavior is absurd and merits ridicule
senses.definitionCN: 言行荒唐、令人嘲弄的人
senses.example: He made a buffoon of himself at the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 他在辩论中出尽了洋相。
senses.why: What begins as deliberate clowning ends as unintentional self-ridicule.
senses.whyCN: 从刻意的插科打诨滑向无意的自取其辱，义项由扮演转为品评。

senses.title: A vulgar jester
senses.definition: one who amuses with coarse, undignified antics
senses.definitionCN: 以粗鄙、有失体统的举动逗乐的人
senses.example: Critics called the satire vulgar buffoonery.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称这种讽刺是粗俗的滑稽把戏。
senses.why: Low comedy was long despised as beneath refined art.
senses.whyCN: 低级滑稽历来被雅艺术轻视，义项带上了贬抑的道德色彩。

intro.en: Buffoon traveled from Italian through French into English, keeping a dance at its core.
intro.cn: buffoon 经由法语自意大利语传入英语，词核始终是一种舞蹈。

items.en: buffare meant to puff; buffone named a prancing jester, from a trotting dance.
items.cn: 意大利语 buffare 义为喷气，buffone 指一种蹦跳舞的滑稽角色。

items.en: bouffon kept the sense of a grotesque comic figure.
items.cn: 法语 bouffon 保留了怪诞滑稽角色之义。

items.en: buffoon entered English for court jesters and low comics.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪 buffoon 进入英语，指宫廷弄臣与低俗滑稽演员。

items.en: buffoonery and buffoonish spread the word through moralistic criticism.
items.cn: buffoonery、buffoonish 随道德批评流行开来。

items.en: buffoon now mocks any public figure acting ridiculously.
items.cn: 如今 buffoon 用以讥讽任何举止荒唐的公众人物。

note.cn: buffoon 与一串 -oon 结尾的词押韵，并与整个「小丑」词族为邻。

entries.definitionCN: 闺房，拼形相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a comic performer; a fool

normal.cn: 词根 buffare 意为喷气、吹气。

normal.en: Endings -oon mark disguise words: harlequin, pantaloon, buffoon.
normal.cn: -oon 结尾常是乔装角色：harlequin、pantaloon、buffoon。

normal.en: Play the buffoon is the set phrase for clowning.
normal.cn: play the buffoon 是「扮丑」的固定说法。

normal.en: Buffoonery adds -ery, the suffix of behavior.
normal.cn: buffoonery 加 -ery，即「行为」后缀。

normal.en: Court jesters were the original professional buffoons.
normal.cn: 宫廷弄臣是最早的职业丑角。

abstract.en: See a man slip on a banana peel on purpose.
abstract.cn: 看见有人故意踩上香蕉皮滑倒。

abstract.en: Hear a whoopee cushion burst in a silent hall.
abstract.cn: 听一声屁垫在肃静的大厅里炸响。

abstract.en: Feel your face stretch into a clown's painted grin.
abstract.cn: 感受脸被小丑油彩扯出的咧嘴笑。

examples.en: The politician dismissed his rival as a buffoon.
examples.cn: 那位政客讥讽对手不过是个丑角。

examples.en: Shakespeare's fools were buffoons with wisdom underneath.
examples.cn: 莎士比亚笔下的弄臣是内藏智慧的丑角。

examples.en: He played the buffoon until the teacher lost patience.
examples.cn: 他一直扮丑作怪，直到老师失去耐心。

definition_zh: 过时的；不再使用的；被淘汰的；废弃的；（词、法规）已不通用的
definition_en: no longer used or accepted because something newer has replaced it
core_image: 仓库角落一箱旧式接口零件还在，新到的设备上已经找不到能插进去的孔
scene: 仓库角落里还堆着一箱旧式接口零件，新到的设备上已经找不到能插进去的孔。 The warehouse still holds obsolete connectors that no current device accepts.
sceneCN: 这里指已被淘汰、不再使用（第 1 个义项：不再使用的）；句意为仓库里仍存着没有一台现役设备能接上的过时接口件。图中可辨识物件：仓库角落、旧接口零件箱、新设备、无法插入的端口。

pos.zh: 过时的；不再使用的；废弃的；被淘汰的
（少用）使废弃；使过时

derivatives.zh: 由该词干加表示过程的名词尾构成，义为「废弃；淘汰过程」
由该词干加表示「正在……的」词尾构成，义为「正逐渐淘汰的」
由该词干加动词尾构成，义为「逐渐废弃；变得过时」
由「计划的」与该名词构成，义为「有计划地使产品过时」

senses.title: No longer used
senses.definition: no longer used because something newer has taken its place
senses.definitionCN: 由于有更新之物取代而不再使用
senses.example: Gas lamps became obsolete when electric light reached the streets.
senses.exampleCN: 电灯进入街道后，煤气灯就不再使用了。
senses.why: The Latin participle means grown out of use, and this sense is its plainest survival.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「变得不被使用」，这一义项是最直白的延续。

senses.title: A word fallen out of use
senses.definition: a word that people no longer say except when reading old texts
senses.definitionCN: 人们除读旧文外已不再说的词
senses.example: The dictionary marks the word as obsolete after 1700.
senses.exampleCN: 词典把这个词标为 1700 年后已废弃。
senses.why: Language change produces the same effect as machinery: the old form still exists, but nobody reaches for it.
senses.whyCN: 语言变化造成的效果和机器一样：旧形式还在，只是没人再去取用。

senses.title: A rule no longer in force
senses.definition: a regulation that has been replaced or withdrawn
senses.definitionCN: 已被替换或撤销的规章
senses.example: The clause is obsolete and should be struck from the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款已失效，应从合同中删去。
senses.why: Law keeps obsolete clauses on paper long after practice has left them.
senses.whyCN: 实践早已离开的条款，法律仍让它们留在纸上。

senses.title: A superseded machine
senses.definition: equipment that newer models have made impractical to keep
senses.definitionCN: 新机型使其继续保留已不实用的设备
senses.example: Spare parts for the obsolete printer now cost more than a new one.
senses.exampleCN: 那台淘汰打印机的配件，现在比买新的还贵。
senses.why: A machine is obsolete when fixing it costs more than replacing it.
senses.whyCN: 当修理比替换更贵，机器就被淘汰了。

senses.title: An idea left behind
senses.definition: a belief that no longer fits current knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 不再符合当今知识的看法
senses.example: The idea that memory is a single store is obsolete.
senses.exampleCN: 认为记忆是单一仓库的看法已经过时。
senses.why: Ideas age without breaking, which is why the word fits them so well.
senses.whyCN: 观念不会坏，只会老，所以这个词用在他们身上特别贴切。

senses.title: Old stock still on the shelf
senses.definition: goods kept in storage although nobody now buys them
senses.definitionCN: 虽仍存放、如今却无人购买的货物
senses.example: The shop wrote off its obsolete stock at the end of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 商店在年末把积压的淘汰存货核销。
senses.why: Stock becomes obsolete while it is still perfectly new in the box.
senses.whyCN: 存货在盒子里还崭新时，就已经成了淘汰货。

senses.title: A retired unit or currency
senses.definition: a unit of money or measure that has been withdrawn
senses.definitionCN: 已被停用的货币或计量单位
senses.example: Prices were still quoted in an obsolete currency after the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 改革之后，标价仍用已经停用的货币。
senses.why: Money and measures can be withdrawn by decree, and then the word is official.
senses.whyCN: 货币与单位可由法令停用，这时这个词是官方用语。

senses.title: A practice abandoned
senses.definition: a way of doing things that has been given up
senses.definitionCN: 已经被放弃的做事方式
senses.example: Hand-copying records by ink became obsolete once the database went live.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库上线后，用墨水手抄记录的做法就被废弃了。
senses.why: A habit disappears when the tool that carried it disappears first.
senses.whyCN: 当承载习惯的工具先消失，习惯也随之消失。

intro.en: Obsolete comes from Latin obsoletus, grown old or worn out, the past participle of obsolescere, to fall into disuse. The verb is usually explained as ob-, away, plus solere, to be accustomed, though the exact force of the prefix is described differently by different sources. English took the adjective in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 obsoletus「变旧、用坏」，是动词 obsolescere「渐不用」的过去分词。该动词通常解释为「离开」加「习惯于」，但前缀的具体作用各家说法不一。英语在十六世纪吸收了该形容词。

items.en: Solere meant to be accustomed or to be in the habit, and it stands behind the idea of usual practice.
items.cn: 这个词意为「习惯于、常有此习」，是「惯常做法」这一观念背后的词。

items.en: The verb meant to wear out or fall out of use, and its prefix suggests moving away from what was usual.
items.cn: 该动词意为用坏或渐不用，其前缀暗示从惯常状态离开。

items.en: The participle described what had already grown old and was no longer wanted.
items.cn: 该分词形容已经变旧、不再被需要之物。

items.en: French used the adjective for words and customs that had dropped away.
items.cn: 法语用它指已经消失的词与习俗。

items.en: English extended it from words to machines, laws and ideas.
items.cn: 英语把它从词语扩展到机器、法规与观念。

items.en: Manufacturing gave it the compound planned obsolescence; the phrase's first year is uncertain.
items.cn: 制造业给出复合说法「有计划地淘汰」；该说法首见的年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the grown-out-of-use root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of being out of date. The note warns that absolute is a look-alike from an unrelated root.
note.cn: 第一组共享「用旧而废」词根或形近；第二组指其他「过时」的说法。这里提醒：形近的「绝对」一词出自不相干的词根。

entries.definition: The process of becoming outdated.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐过时的过程。

entries.definition: In the process of becoming obsolete.
entries.definitionCN: 指正在走向淘汰的。

entries.definition: To grow obsolete.
entries.definitionCN: 指变得过时。

entries.definition: Complete and unconditional; it comes from a verb meaning to loosen or set free, not from being accustomed.
entries.definitionCN: 指完全且无条件的；出自表示「解开、释放」的动词，与「习惯于」无关。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned but possibly still usable.
entries.definitionCN: 指样式老但可能仍可使用。

entries.definition: Very old and no longer suitable, often said of systems.
entries.definitionCN: 指非常老旧且已不适用，常用于制度。

entries.definition: No longer in fashion or no longer the accepted way.
entries.definitionCN: 指不再流行或不再是被接受的方式。

entries.definition: No longer existing or operating, said of organizations.
entries.definitionCN: 指已不存在或停止运作，用于机构。

entries.definition: Replaced by something that does the job better.
entries.definitionCN: 指被做得更好的东西取代。

entries.definition: Belonging to an earlier period and retained only in special contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于较早时期、只在特殊语境中保留。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the box of connectors, the gas lamp, the struck-out contract clause and the written-off stock.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用那箱接口件、煤气灯、被划掉的合同条款与核销的存货。

normal.en: Obsolete does not mean broken; it means nobody reaches for it any more.
normal.cn: 「过时」不等于坏了，而是没人再去取用它。

normal.en: A gas lamp still lights, but the street is wired for electricity.
normal.cn: 煤气灯仍能亮，可街上已经通了电。

normal.en: The word and the machine share one fate: both are outgrown.
normal.cn: 词语与机器命运相同：都被长过了头。

normal.en: Planned obsolescence is obsolescence with a schedule and a budget.
normal.cn: 「有计划地淘汰」，就是带着日程与预算的淘汰。

normal.en: Absolute looks close but belongs to loosening, not to growing old.
normal.cn: 形近的那个词属于「解开」，不属于「变旧」。

abstract.en: Usefulness is a relationship between a thing and a moment, and moments move.
abstract.cn: 有用是物与时刻之间的关系，而时刻会走。

abstract.en: Every generation inherits tools it must first learn to stop using.
abstract.cn: 每一代人都继承了一批必须先学会不再使用的工具。

abstract.en: What becomes obsolete usually leaves a word behind that outlives it.
abstract.cn: 被淘汰的东西，往往留下一个比它活得更久的词。

examples.en: The format is obsolete, and the archive can no longer open the files.
examples.cn: 这种格式已经过时，档案馆再也打不开那些文件。

examples.en: New scanning software rendered the old index cards obsolete overnight.
examples.cn: 新的扫描软件一夜之间让旧索引卡被淘汰。

examples.en: Using that term today sounds obsolete even in legal writing.
examples.cn: 今天再用那个词，即便在法律文书里也显得过时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥伯索利特」：旧东西还在架上，只是没人再伸手去拿，慢慢就「废」了

root: 源于拉丁语表示「习惯于」的动词，其复合动词义为「渐不用、用坏」，过去分词义为「变旧废弃的」，经法语进入英语。该前缀的具体作用各家解释不一。十六世纪进入英语；「有计划地淘汰」一语首见年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow disuse: an unused thing, a dead word, a withdrawn rule, a superseded machine, a left-behind idea, unsold stock, a retired unit, and an abandoned practice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「不再使用」展开：闲置之物、废弃的词、撤销的规定、被取代的机器、被抛下的观念、卖不掉的存货、停用的单位与放弃的做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the box of connectors that no new machine has a port for.
core.cn: 核心意象：一箱接口件，新机器上找不到能插的孔。

branches.en: THE RETIRED THING: an object or machine that newer things replaced.
branches.cn: 退役之物：被更新之物取代的器物或机器。

branches.en: THE RETIRED WORD AND IDEA: what people no longer say or believe.
branches.cn: 退役的词与观念：人们不再说、也不再信的东西。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE LEFT ON PAPER: a rule that practice has already abandoned.
branches.cn: 留在纸上的条款：实践早已放弃的规则。

branches.en: THE SHELF AND THE HABIT: stock nobody buys, practices nobody follows.
branches.cn: 货架与习惯：无人购买的存货、无人沿用的做法。

branches.en: THE WITHDRAWN UNIT: money or measures taken out of use by decree.
branches.cn: 撤销的单位：由法令停用的货币或计量单位。

intro.en: Obsolete is a Latin participle used as an English adjective; its family covers the process of going out of use and the schedule that produces it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁分词用作英语形容词；词族覆盖「走向废弃」的过程，以及制造这一过程的日程。

latinIntro.en: Latin solere and obsolescere supply the habit and the falling away from it; the participle obsoletus gives the English form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「习惯于」与「渐不用」提供「习惯」与「离开习惯」两层意思；分词给出英语形态。

items.exampleCN: 它提供「惯常做法」的意思。

items.example: It marks movement away from the usual.
items.exampleCN: 它标出「离开常态」的方向。

items.example: The verb of decay behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是词背后的「衰废」动词。

items.example: It gives the English adjective directly.
items.exampleCN: 它直接给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It forms the rare verb obsolesce.
items.exampleCN: 它构成少用的动词「变得过时」。

items.example: A commercial phrase built on the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 由该形容词构成的商业说法。

definition_zh: adj. 勇敢的，有胆量的
definition_en: brave enough to face danger or pain
core_image: 心里发抖，脚步仍往前走
scene: 明知危险，他还是独自站了出来。 He was courageous enough to speak up alone.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：courageous 指勇敢的；句意是他足够勇敢，独自公开发言。

pos.zh: 勇敢的；有胆量的

senses.title: Facing danger
senses.definition: able to face danger without backing away
senses.definitionCN: 面对危险也不退缩
senses.example: The firefighter made a courageous rescue.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员完成了一次勇敢的救援。
senses.why: A step forward while fear shouts stop.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧喊停，脚步仍向前。

senses.title: Bold in speech
senses.definition: willing to say what is right despite pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下仍敢说出正确的话
senses.example: She gave a courageous speech.
senses.exampleCN: 她作了一次勇敢的演讲。
senses.why: A small voice in a loud room.
senses.whyCN: 喧闹房间里的一个小声音。

senses.title: Strong in spirit
senses.definition: strong in spirit when life is hard
senses.definitionCN: 艰难时刻精神依然坚强
senses.example: He stayed courageous through the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 他生病期间始终保持勇敢。
senses.why: A candle burning in the wind.
senses.whyCN: 风里不灭的蜡烛。

intro.en: Courageous comes from Latin cor, heart, through Old French corage, courage, plus the suffix -ous, full of.
intro.cn: courageous 源自拉丁语 cor（心），经古法语 corage（勇气），加后缀 -ous（充满）构成。
