definition_zh: 一贯地；始终如一地；持续稳定地
definition_en: in a way that stays the same over time and does not change from one case to another
core_image: 节拍器以完全相同的间隔敲击，一次也不快、一次也不慢
scene: 这里指「一贯地」。 The lab technician consistently records the temperature at the same hour every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 consistently 是「一贯地、始终如一地」（第 1 个义项：以同样的方式反复做）；句意：实验室技术员每天早上都在同一时间记录温度，从不间断。图中可辨识物件：温度计、记录本、挂钟、实验台。

pos.zh: 一贯地；始终如一地；持续稳定地

senses.title: In the same way every time
senses.definition: in a way that does not change from one occasion to the next
senses.definitionCN: 以不随场合改变的方式
senses.example: The lab technician consistently records the temperature at the same hour every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室技术员每天早上都在同一时间记录温度。
senses.why: Consistently is consistent + -ly. Consistent comes from the present-participle stem of consist, from Latin consistere 'stand firm'. An action done consistently is an action that keeps standing in the same place, occasion after occasion.
senses.whyCN: consistently 是 consistent + -ly。consistent 来自 consist 的现在分词词干，而 consist 出自拉丁语 consistere“站稳”。一贯地做一件事，就是让这个动作在一次次场合中始终站在同一个位置。

senses.title: Consistently high: keeping a high level
senses.titleCN: 持续保持高水平：长期维持高位
senses.definition: remaining at a high level over a period, without falling
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内保持高水平而不下降
senses.example: The school has consistently high graduation rates.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校的毕业率持续保持在高位。
senses.why: The -ly adverb measures how an adjective holds over time. A consistently high level is one that stands firm at the top instead of rising and falling; the 'standing' image is applied to a position on a scale.
senses.whyCN: -ly 副词衡量一个形容词状态在时间中如何维持。持续偏高的水平，就是稳稳站在高位而不上下起伏；“站立”的形象被用到了刻度上的位置。

senses.title: Consistently apply: use the same rule everywhere
senses.titleCN: 一致适用：到处使用同一规则
senses.definition: to apply a rule, standard, or method in the same way to every case
senses.definitionCN: 把规则、标准或方法以相同方式用于每个情形
senses.example: The referee consistently applied the new rule throughout the season.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判在整个赛季一致适用新规则。
senses.why: Consistent originally meant 'standing together'. When a rule is applied, the cases must all stand together under one standard. The -ly adverb says the standard is not bent from case to case.
senses.whyCN: consistent 原意是“站在一起”。适用规则时，所有情形都必须站在同一标准之下。-ly 副词说明这个标准不会因情形不同而弯曲。

senses.title: Perform consistently: deliver a steady standard
senses.titleCN: 稳定表现：交付稳定水准
senses.definition: to perform at a steady level without large swings in quality
senses.definitionCN: 以稳定水平表现，质量没有大幅波动
senses.example: She performs consistently well under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 她在压力下表现始终稳定。
senses.why: Performance varies across events, and consistency is what makes those events 'stand together'. The adverb marks the absence of swings: each showing holds the same level as the last.
senses.whyCN: 表现会随场次变化，而 consistency 就是让这些场次“站在一起”的东西。这个副词标记的正是没有波动：每一次表现都与上一次保持同一水平。

senses.title: Consistently follow: keep obeying a rule
senses.definition: to keep following a rule, instruction, or procedure without exception
senses.definitionCN: 无例外地一直遵照规则、指示或程序
senses.example: All staff have consistently followed the safety procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 全体员工始终遵循安全程序。
senses.why: Following is a repeated act, and -ly says the repetition never breaks. The base image of standing firm becomes temporal: the behaviour stays in line instead of drifting away.
senses.whyCN: 遵循是反复发生的动作，-ly 说明这种重复从未中断。“站稳”的词基形象在此变成时间性的：行为始终留在线上，而不是漂走。

senses.title: Consistently accurate: keeping the same precision
senses.titleCN: 始终保持准确：精度一直不变
senses.definition: remaining accurate to the same degree on every occasion
senses.definitionCN: 每次都以相同程度保持准确
senses.example: The old scale has remained consistently accurate for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧秤十年来始终保持准确。
senses.why: Accuracy can drift; consistently says it does not. The suffix -ly converts 'standing firm' into a manner of measurement: the readings keep standing at the true value.
senses.whyCN: 准确度会漂移；consistently 说明它没有漂。后缀 -ly 把“站稳”转成一种测量方式：读数一直站在真值上。

senses.title: Consistently better: always ahead in comparison
senses.titleCN: 一直更好：比较中始终领先
senses.definition: better than the alternative on every or almost every occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在每次或几乎每次场合都比另一选择更好
senses.example: Their new model has consistently outperformed the older one.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的新模型一直比旧模型表现更好。
senses.why: With a comparative, -ly says the comparison keeps the same result. The gap may be small, but it never reverses; that is 'standing firm' applied to a ranking.
senses.whyCN: 与比较级连用时，-ly 说明比较结果始终不变。差距也许不大，但从不反转；这就是“站稳”用在排名上。

senses.title: Consistently support: back something at every turn
senses.titleCN: 始终支持：每次都站在同一边
senses.definition: to support a person, plan, or policy on every relevant occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在每个相关场合都支持某人、某计划或某政策
senses.example: The mayor has consistently supported the housing project.
senses.exampleCN: 市长始终支持这个住房项目。
senses.why: Support is a stance, and a stance can be held. Consistently turns that stance into a long-held position: the person keeps standing on the same side of the question.
senses.whyCN: 支持是一种立场，而立场可以被“守住”。consistently 把这种立场变成长期保持的位置：此人在问题上始终站在同一边。

senses.title: Consistently refuse: say no every time
senses.definition: to refuse something every time it is proposed or offered
senses.definitionCN: 每当某事被提出或提供时都拒绝
senses.example: The committee has consistently refused to release the minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会一贯拒绝公布会议记录。
senses.why: Refusal can be a one-off act; consistently makes it a settled policy. The adverb adds the same temporal firmness: the answer stands firm each time the question returns.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝可以是一次性动作；consistently 把它变成既定政策。副词增添了同样的时间性坚定：每当问题再次出现，答案都稳稳不变。

intro.en: Consistently is consistent + -ly, where consistent itself comes from consist plus -ent. The chain is Latin consistere 'stand firm' → English consist → consistent → consistently. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: consistently 是 consistent + -ly，而 consistent 本身来自 consist 加 -ent。链条是拉丁语 consistere“站稳” → 英语 consist → consistent → consistently。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Latin consistere means 'to take one's stand, stand firm; to be composed of'. It is con- 'together' + sistere 'to stand'. The physical image is a group of things holding a position together.
items.cn: 拉丁语 consistere 意为“站定、站稳；由……构成”。它是 con-“一起” + sistere“站立”。具体形象是若干事物一起守住一个位置。

items.en: English consist is borrowed from consistere. Its early sense 'to have a settled position' yields the modern 'to be made up of', which is the base of the whole family.
items.cn: 英语 consist 借自 consistere。早期“占据稳定位置”的义项发展出现代“由……构成”，后者成为整个词族的基础。

items.en: Consist's present-participle stem consistent- plus -ent (Latin -ent-, adjective suffix) gives consistent: literally 'standing firm, holding together'. The suffix makes a quality adjective out of the verb's action.
items.cn: consist 的现在分词词干 consistent- 加 -ent（拉丁语 -ent-，形容词后缀）构成 consistent：字面是“站稳的、保持在一起的”。后缀把动词动作变成性质形容词。

items.en: Consistent + -ly (Old English -lice) forms consistently, 'in a consistent manner'. This is the key step of this entry: the adjective's stable quality becomes the manner of an action.
items.cn: consistent + -ly（古英语 -lice）构成 consistently，意为“以一致的方式”。这是本条目的关键一步：形容词的稳定性质变成了动作的方式。

items.en: The literal 'standing firm' first described physical position, then character, then repeated behaviour. With -ly the emphasis moves to time: the same standard is held across many occasions, not just at one moment.
items.cn: 字面的“站稳”先描述物理位置，再描述性格，最后描述重复行为。加 -ly 后重心转向时间：同一标准在众多场合中被保持，而不只维持于一瞬。

items.en: Modern English uses consistently with verbs of performance, application, support and refusal, and with comparatives such as 'consistently better'. The word has become a general marker of reliable repetition.
items.cn: 现代英语把 consistently 用于表现、适用、支持、拒绝等动词，也用于 consistently better 这类比较级。这个词已成为“可靠重复”的通用标记。

note.en: The first group lists close spellings and family forms; the second lists adverbs with a similar meaning.
note.cn: 第一组列出拼写相近及同族形式；第二组列出意思相近的副词。

entries.definition: always behaving or happening in the same way. It is the adjective behind consistently.
entries.definitionCN: 始终以相同方式行事或发生的。它是 consistently 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: to be made up of particular parts. It is the root verb of the family, not an adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 由特定部分构成。它是这个词族的根动词，不是副词。

entries.definition: in a forceful, demanding way. It comes from insist, a different prefix and a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 以强硬、要求的方式。它来自 insist，前缀不同，意思也不同。

entries.definition: at fixed intervals or on a habitual basis. It stresses timing rather than sameness of quality.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔或习惯性地。它强调时间规律，而不是品质相同。

entries.definition: in the same way in every case. It is closer to 'identically' than consistently is.
entries.definitionCN: 在每种情况下都以相同方式。它比 consistently 更接近“完全相同地”。

entries.definition: in a continuous, even way. It often describes gradual change or pace.
entries.definitionCN: 以连续、平稳的方式。它常描述逐渐变化或节奏。

entries.definition: in a way that can be trusted to happen or work. It stresses dependability rather than sameness.
entries.definitionCN: 以可被信赖会发生或奏效的方式。它强调可靠，而不是相同。

entries.definition: always, with no exception. It is stronger and more absolute than consistently.
entries.definitionCN: 总是，没有例外。它比 consistently 更强、更绝对。

normalIntro.en: These associations use the real consist family, the real -ent and -ly chain, and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想使用真实的 consist 词族、真实的 -ent 与 -ly 链条，以及真实搭配。

normal.en: consist means 'stand together'; consistent means 'standing together'; consistently means 'in a standing-together way'. The family keeps one picture.
normal.cn: consist 意为“站在一起”；consistent 意为“站得住的”；consistently 意为“以站得住的方式”。整个词族保持同一个画面。

normal.en: consist → consistent → consistently is a clean three-step ladder: verb, adjective, adverb.
normal.cn: consist → consistent → consistently 是一架清晰的三级梯子：动词、形容词、副词。

normal.en: The common frames are consistently high, consistently perform, consistently apply, consistently support, consistently refuse.
normal.cn: 常见框架有 consistently high、consistently perform、consistently apply、consistently support、consistently refuse。

normal.en: Do not confuse consistent with constant: constant means 'never stopping', consistent means 'not changing shape from case to case'.
normal.cn: 不要把 consistent 与 constant 混淆：constant 是“从不停歇”，consistent 是“在不同情形下不变形”。

normal.en: With comparatives, consistently means 'every time, not just once': consistently better, consistently ahead.
normal.cn: 与比较级连用时，consistently 表示“每次都如此，而不只一次”：consistently better、consistently ahead。

abstract.en: Picture a metronome: its ticks are the repeated occasions, and consistently is the identical interval between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个节拍器：它的敲击就是一次次场合，而 consistently 就是它们之间完全相同的间隔。

abstract.en: The word is a line drawn through many points. Each point may differ, but the line does not bend.
abstract.cn: 这个词是穿过许多点的一条线。每个点可以不同，但线本身不弯。

abstract.en: All nine senses keep one promise: what happened last time will happen again in the same way.
abstract.cn: 九个义项都信守同一个承诺：上次怎样发生，这次还以同样的方式发生。

examples.en: The team has consistently delivered high-quality work.
examples.cn: 这个团队一直交付高质量的工作。

examples.en: The same rules must be consistently applied to every applicant.
examples.cn: 同样的规则必须一致适用于每位申请者。

examples.en: She has consistently refused to discuss the matter.
examples.cn: 她一贯拒绝讨论此事。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯细思坦特利”——肯细细思量，站得稳、做得利落 → consistently 一贯地

root: consist（拉丁 consistere“站稳、站在一起”）+ -ent（形容词后缀）+ -ly（副词后缀）：以始终站得住、不改变的方式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of consistently all describe repetition without drift. The repeated thing may be a level, a rule, a performance, a reading, a comparison, a stance, or a refusal.
sensesIntro.cn: consistently 的九个义项都描述“重复而不漂移”。重复的对象可以是水平、规则、表现、读数、比较、立场或拒绝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metronome ticking at exactly the same interval.
core.cn: 核心意象：节拍器以完全相同的间隔敲击。

branches.en: GENERAL HABIT AND OBEDIENCE: doing or following the same thing each time.
branches.cn: 一般习惯与遵从：每次都做或遵循同一件事。

branches.en: LEVEL AND PERFORMANCE: keeping a high or steady standard across events.
branches.cn: 水平与表现：在各次事件中保持高而稳的水准。

branches.en: RULES AND ACCURACY: applying one standard everywhere, and holding the same precision.
branches.cn: 规则与准确：到处适用同一标准，并保持同样的精度。

branches.en: COMPARISON AND REFUSAL: always ahead in a ranking, or always saying no.
branches.cn: 比较与拒绝：在排名中始终领先，或始终说不。

branches.en: POLITICAL STANCE: supporting the same side at every turn.
branches.cn: 立场：在每个场合都支持同一边。

intro.en: Consistently is the end of a three-stage suffix chain: -ent turns the verb consist into the adjective consistent, and -ly turns that adjective into an adverb of manner. No prefix is involved.
intro.cn: consistently 是三级后缀链条的末端：-ent 把动词 consist 变成形容词 consistent，-ly 再把形容词变成方式副词。这里不涉及前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is consistere 'stand firm', built from con- 'together' + sistere 'to stand'. Latin supplies the base and -ent; -ly is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 consistere“站稳”，由 con-“一起” + sistere“站立”构成。拉丁语提供词基和 -ent；-ly 是英语本族后缀。

definition_zh: 决定性地；无可辩驳地；确凿无疑地
definition_en: in a way that settles a question or proves something so strongly that no doubt remains
core_image: 一只手掌按下盒盖，接缝彻底合拢
scene: 这里指「决定性地」。 In the courtroom, the DNA report conclusively showed that the defendant had not been at the scene.
sceneCN: 这里 conclusively 是「确凿无疑地」（第 2 个义项：以确凿证据证明）；句意：法庭上，DNA 报告确凿无疑地表明被告当时不在现场。图中可辨识物件：法庭、DNA 检测报告、被告席、法官、证物袋。

pos.zh: 决定性地；无可辩驳地；确凿无疑地

senses.title: Settling the matter beyond dispute
senses.titleCN: 决定性地：让争议无从继续
senses.definition: in a manner that ends doubt or argument about a question
senses.definitionCN: 以结束疑问或争论的方式
senses.example: The review conclusively settled the question of who had approved the payment.
senses.exampleCN: 这次复核决定性地弄清了是谁批准了这笔付款。
senses.why: claudere means 'to close'. The -ive suffix gives the adjective the quality of closing, and -ly turns that quality into the manner of an action. To act conclusively is to act in a way that shuts the question.
senses.whyCN: claudere 意为“关闭”。-ive 让形容词带上“关闭”的性质，-ly 再把这种性质变成动作的方式。所谓 conclusively 地行动，就是以把问题合上的方式行动。

senses.title: Proving by hard evidence
senses.titleCN: 确凿证明地：用证据封口
senses.definition: by evidence strong enough to remove every reasonable doubt
senses.definitionCN: 以足以排除一切合理怀疑的证据
senses.example: Tests conclusively proved that the river water contained harmful bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 检测确凿地证明河水里含有有害细菌。
senses.why: The base image is a container with openings. Evidence fills each opening until nothing more can get in, and -ly names the strength with which the case is sealed.
senses.whyCN: 基础意象是一个有开口的容器。证据把每个开口都填满，直到再没有任何东西能进入；-ly 说明的就是封口的力量。

senses.title: Closing a debate
senses.titleCN: 终结争论地：把对话关上
senses.definition: in a way that brings an argument or discussion to an end
senses.definitionCN: 以使争论或讨论结束的方式
senses.example: Her last piece of evidence conclusively ended the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 她最后的证据终结了这场争论。
senses.why: An argument is treated as a space that stays open while people keep talking. Closing it ends the exchange, so the adverb names the manner of that closing.
senses.whyCN: 争论被看成一个只要人还在说就一直敞开的空间。把它关上就结束了交流，副词描述的正是这种关上的方式。

senses.title: Clearly and without ambiguity
senses.titleCN: 明确无疑地：没有第二种读法
senses.definition: in a clear way that cannot reasonably be interpreted differently
senses.definitionCN: 以清楚、不会被合理作他解的方式
senses.example: The data conclusively show a steady decline in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 数据明确无疑地显示出销量的持续下滑。
senses.why: A closed surface has no ambiguous opening. The adverb extends the 'no gap' image from containers to meaning: the statement is shut against a second reading.
senses.whyCN: 合拢的表面没有暧昧的开口。副词把这个“不留缝”的意象从容器扩展到意义：这句话对第二种读法是封闭的。

senses.title: A final legal determination
senses.titleCN: 最终判定地：法律上的定案
senses.definition: as a final and official determination by a court or authority
senses.definitionCN: 作为法院或主管机关的最终正式判定
senses.example: The court conclusively determined where the property line lay.
senses.exampleCN: 法院最终判定确定了地界线的位置。
senses.why: Legal language borrows the same seal: a ruling is 'final' when the matter is closed. The -ly adverb marks the official manner in which the record is shut.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言借用了同一个“封印”：当事情被关上，裁决就是“终局”的。-ly 副词标明的正是案卷被合上的官方方式。

senses.title: Showing by conclusion
senses.titleCN: 结论性地展示：把终点摆出来
senses.definition: in a presentational way that displays a chain of reasoning up to its end
senses.definitionCN: 以展示推理链条直至终点的呈现方式
senses.example: The chart conclusively displays the order in which the events occurred.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图表结论性地展示了事件发生的顺序。
senses.why: The sense is presentational: to show conclusively is to lay out the chain so that its end is visibly shut, with no missing link.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项偏重“呈现”：conclusively 地展示，就是把链条铺开，让它的末端 visibly 合上，中间没有缺环。

senses.title: Ruling out alternatives
senses.titleCN: 决定性地排除：逐扇关门
senses.definition: so completely as to eliminate all other possibilities
senses.definitionCN: 以彻底到排除其他一切可能性的方式
senses.example: The fingerprints conclusively ruled out the first suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 指纹决定性地排除了第一名嫌疑人。
senses.why: Exclusion works like shutting doors: each alternative is closed off. The adverb describes the completeness of that closing, leaving one possibility standing.
senses.whyCN: 排除就像逐扇关门：每个替代可能都被关上。副词描述的是这种关闭的彻底程度，最后只留下一种可能。

senses.title: Establishing firmly
senses.titleCN: 决定性地确立：钉牢不留松动
senses.definition: in a way that fixes a fact, link, or principle firmly and permanently
senses.definitionCN: 以牢固而永久地固定事实、联系或原则的方式
senses.example: The experiment conclusively established a link between the two variables.
senses.exampleCN: 这项实验决定性地确立了两个变量之间的联系。
senses.why: To establish is to fix something in place. Conclusively adds that the fixing is sealed, so later argument cannot loosen it.
senses.whyCN: establish 是把某物固定在位置上。conclusively 追加的是“封住”这层意思，使后来的论证无法把它撬松。

senses.title: In the manner of a last word
senses.titleCN: 以最后结论的方式：说完再无可答
senses.definition: as a closing statement that leaves nothing further to be said
senses.definitionCN: 作为不再给人留下回应空间的收尾陈述
senses.example: He spoke conclusively, and nobody in the room raised another objection.
senses.exampleCN: 他以最后结论的口吻说话，房间里没有人再提出异议。
senses.why: This is the social side of claudere: the speaker closes the conversation. The -ly suffix marks the manner of speaking that leaves nothing to answer.
senses.whyCN: 这是 claudere 的社会性一面：说话者把对话关上。-ly 后缀标明的正是那种不给人留回答余地的说话方式。

intro.en: Conclusively is a transparent modern derivative: the Latin verb concludere supplies the meaning, -ive turns it into an adjective, and -ly turns that adjective into an adverb. Dates for the English stages are approximate.
intro.cn: conclusively 是一个结构透明的现代派生词：拉丁动词 concludere 提供意义，-ive 把它变成形容词，-ly 再把形容词变成副词。各英语阶段的年代为大致估计。

items.en: concludere meant 'to shut up, enclose, bring to an end'. Its two parts are con- 'together' and claudere 'to close'; the literal picture is a space shut on every side.
items.cn: concludere 意为“关闭、围合、使结束”。两部分是 con-“一起”和 claudere“关闭”；字面画面是一个四面都合上的空间。

items.en: The past participle conclusus supplied the stem conclus-, which English uses in conclusion, conclusive and conclusively. The stem carries the result 'already shut', not the act of shutting.
items.cn: 过去分词 conclusus 提供了词干 conclus-，英语在 conclusion、conclusive、conclusively 中使用它。这个词干携带的是“已经关上”的结果，而不是关闭的动作。

items.en: conclusive adds -ive, from Latin -ivus, meaning 'having the nature of'. An argument that is conclusive has the nature of a closing: it shuts the case.
items.cn: conclusive 加上 -ive（来自拉丁 -ivus），意为“具有……性质的”。一个 conclusive 的论证具有“关闭”的性质：它把案子合上。

items.en: The move from 'closing' to 'decisive' is metaphorical. Once the last gap is shut, nothing can enter to reopen the question, so 'closed' becomes 'beyond dispute'.
items.cn: 从“关闭”到“决定性”的转变是隐喻性的。最后的缝隙一旦合上，就没有东西能进入重新打开问题，于是“已关闭”变成“无可争辩”。

items.en: conclusive + -ly, from Old English -lice, makes an adverb of manner. It answers 'how' rather than 'what': the proof closes the matter in a conclusive way.
items.cn: conclusive + -ly（来自古英语 -lice）构成方式副词。它回答的是“怎样”，而不是“什么”：这项证明以 conclusive 的方式把事情合上。

items.en: Modern usage is strongest in law and science, where conclusively prove, demonstrate or rule out marks evidence that leaves no room for doubt. The exact first recorded date of the adverb is uncertain.
items.cn: 现代用法最集中于法律和科学语境，conclusively prove、demonstrate 或 rule out 标记的是不留怀疑空间的证据。该副词最早的确切记录年代存疑。

note.en: The first group contains spelling neighbours built on the same Latin verb; the second contains words that come close in meaning but differ in what they emphasize.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在同一拉丁动词上的形近词；第二组是意思接近、但强调点不同的词。

entries.definition: Stating a conclusion without giving evidence; in law, a conclusory statement is a bare assertion. The -ory suffix marks a tendency or result, not proof.
entries.definitionCN: 只下结论而不给证据的；在法律上，conclusory statement 是未经论证的断言。-ory 后缀标记倾向或结果，并不表示证明。

entries.definition: Including everything or everyone. It comes from includere, in- 'in' + claudere 'close', a cousin of concludere.
entries.definitionCN: 包含一切的；包括所有相关人或物的。它来自 includere（in-“向内”+ claudere“关闭”），是 concludere 的同族词。

entries.definition: Excluding others; restricted to a particular group. From excludere, ex- 'out' + claudere 'close'.
entries.definitionCN: 排他的；仅限于特定群体的。来自 excludere（ex-“向外”+ claudere“关闭”）。

entries.definition: in a way that is final and cannot be changed; it stresses official finality more than evidential force.
entries.definitionCN: 以最终、不可更改的方式；它强调官方意义上的终局性，而非证据力度。

entries.definition: in a way that decides an outcome or contest; it points to the effect on a result rather than to proof.
entries.definitionCN: 以决定结果或胜负的方式；它指向对结局的影响，而不是对证据的证明。

entries.definition: without any doubt; it comments on certainty, not necessarily on the strength of evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无疑问地；它评论的是确定性，未必是证据的强度。

entries.definition: in a way that persuades people; it concerns the audience's acceptance, while conclusively concerns the state of the question.
entries.definitionCN: 以令人信服的方式；它关注听众是否接受，而 conclusively 关注问题本身是否已被关上。

entries.definition: in a way that cannot be disputed; closest to conclusively, but more often used of facts than of proofs.
entries.definitionCN: 以无可争议的方式；与 conclusively 最接近，但更多用于事实本身，而非证明过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: con- 'together' + claudere 'close': the debater closes the folder and the case together.
normal.cn: con-“一起”+ claudere“关闭”：辩论者把文件夹和案子一起合上。

normal.en: conclusive is an adjective of quality; conclusively is that quality turned into the manner of an action by -ly.
normal.cn: conclusive 是表性质的形容词；conclusively 是 -ly 把这种性质变成动作方式。

normal.en: The standard pairings are conclusively prove, demonstrate and rule out; these show where the word actually lives.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 conclusively prove、demonstrate、rule out；这些搭配显示这个词实际活跃在哪里。

normal.en: conclude, conclusion, conclusive and conclusively all share the same 'shut' stem, so the family reinforces itself.
normal.cn: conclude、conclusion、conclusive、conclusively 都共享同一个“关闭”词干，这个词族彼此强化。

normal.en: inconclusive is the door that will not close: the evidence leaves the question open, and the negative prefix marks that.
normal.cn: inconclusive 是关不上的门：证据让问题继续敞开，否定前缀标记的就是这一点。

abstract.en: Think of a heavy lid pressed down on a box until the seam disappears: that is conclusively.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的盖子压住箱子，直到接缝消失：这就是 conclusively。

abstract.en: Think of the last puzzle piece clicking into place; nothing is missing, so nothing can be added.
abstract.cn: 想象最后一块拼图咔哒落位；什么都不缺，因此也加不进任何东西。

abstract.en: Think of a wax seal stamped on an envelope: the message is closed, and reopening it would break the seal.
abstract.cn: 想象信封上压下一枚火漆印：消息被封住，再打开就会破坏封印。

examples.en: The second experiment conclusively proved that the material conducts electricity.
examples.cn: 第二次实验确凿地证明这种材料能导电。

examples.en: The committee conclusively rejected the proposal after reviewing all the evidence.
examples.cn: 委员会在审阅全部证据后决定性地否决了这项提案。

examples.en: He argued conclusively, leaving his opponent without a reply.
examples.cn: 他的论证无懈可击，让对手无言以对。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯cluding利”——肯（con）把结论（cluding）关进抽屉，利落锁上 → conclusively 决定性地、无可辩驳地

root: 拉丁 concludere“关闭、围合、得出结论”（con-“一起”+ claudere“关闭”）；conclus- 词干 + -ive“有……性质的”+ -ly 副词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one closing gesture: something is shut, and the shutting removes the possibility of another answer.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个“合拢”动作：某物被关上，而这一关就取消了另一个答案存在的可能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lid closing until no gap remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：盖子合拢，直到不留缝隙。

branches.en: CLOSING AND CLARITY: a closed matter and a closed meaning both leave no opening for another reading.
branches.cn: 合拢与清晰：事情合上、意义合上，两者都不给第二种读法留开口。

branches.en: SEALING WITH EVIDENCE: proof fills every gap, and displaying that proof makes the closure visible.
branches.cn: 用证据封口：证据填满每个缝隙，而把证据展示出来则让合拢过程可见。

branches.en: ENDING THE EXCHANGE: closing a debate and speaking the last word are the social form of the same lid.
branches.cn: 结束交流：终结辩论和说最后一句话，是同一只盖子在社会层面的形态。

branches.en: LEGAL FINALITY AND EXCLUSION: a final ruling shuts the case; ruling out shuts each alternative door.
branches.cn: 法律终局与排除：终局裁决关上案卷；排除则逐扇关上替代选项的门。

branches.en: FIRM ESTABLISHMENT: what is established conclusively is fixed as if sealed in place.
branches.cn: 牢固确立：被 conclusively 确立的东西，像被封印固定住一样。

intro.en: Conclusively is built from live English suffixes on a Latin stem: conclusive + -ly. Only -ive and -ly are productive here; con- and claudere are fossilized inside the base.
intro.cn: conclusively 是在拉丁词干上叠加活的英语后缀：conclusive + -ly。这里只有 -ive 和 -ly 有能产性；con- 与 claudere 已凝固在词基内部。

latinIntro.en: Latin claudere 'to close' is the source of a large family: clause, close, closet, closure, include, exclude, conclude. English borrowed the stems at different times, so the root appears as claud-, claus- or clus-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 claudere“关闭”是一个大词族的源头：clause、close、closet、closure、include、exclude、conclude。英语在不同时期借入这些词干，因此词根会以 claud-、claus- 或 clus- 的形式出现。

items.structure: conclus- (stem of concludere) + -ive (having the nature of)
items.meaning: decisive; putting an end to doubt
items.meaningCN: 决定性的；确凿的（-ive 表示“具有……性质”）
items.example: The evidence was conclusive, and the jury reached a verdict in an hour.
items.exampleCN: 证据是决定性的，陪审团一小时内就作出了裁决。

items.meaning: not leading to a clear decision
items.meaningCN: 非决定性的；无定论的（in-“不”+ conclusive）
items.example: The first test was inconclusive, so they ran a second one.
items.exampleCN: 第一次检测没有定论，于是他们又做了一次。

items.meaning: a judgment reached at the end of reasoning
items.meaningCN: 结论；推论的结果（-ion 构成结果或行为名词）
items.example: The report reaches a clear conclusion about the cause of the fire.
items.exampleCN: 报告对火灾原因得出了明确结论。

items.meaning: to bring to an end; to reach a judgment
items.meaningCN: 结束；得出结论（con-“一起”+ claudere“关闭”）
items.example: The investigators concluded that the accident was caused by human error.
items.exampleCN: 调查人员得出结论，事故由人为失误造成。

items.meaningCN: 决定性地；确凿无疑地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The second trial conclusively proved the link.
items.exampleCN: 第二次试验确凿地证明了这一联系。

items.meaningCN: 决定性；确凿性（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The conclusiveness of the evidence surprised even the defence.
items.exampleCN: 证据的决定性连辩方都感到意外。

items.meaning: the act of closing, or a sense of resolution
items.meaningCN: 关闭；了结（-ure 构成结果名词）
items.example: The family finally found closure after the case was solved.
items.exampleCN: 案件告破后，这家人终于得到了心理上的了结。

items.meaning: the act of shutting something out
items.meaningCN: 排除；排斥（ex-“向外”+ clus-“关闭”+ -ion）
items.example: The exclusion of contaminated samples changed the result.
items.exampleCN: 排除受污染的样本改变了结果。

items.meaning: the act of shutting something in; the state of being included
items.meaningCN: 包含；纳入（in-“向内”+ clus-“关闭”+ -ion）
items.example: The inclusion of older data made the trend clearer.
items.exampleCN: 纳入更早的数据让趋势更清楚。

definition_zh: 谐音的；元音韵的；音似的
definition_en: having or showing assonance; having similar vowel sounds
core_image: 几行诗里元音像同一色系的灯次第点亮
scene: 她把两行诗并排写在黑板上，圈出彼此呼应的元音字母。 The assonant vowels in those lines give the verse its music.
sceneCN: 这里 assonant 是「谐音的」（第 1 个义项：元音相似的）；句意为这些诗行里谐和的元音赋予诗句音乐感。

pos.zh: 谐音的；元音韵的
谐音词（语言学）

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「元音韵；谐音」
由同根加动词后缀构成，义为「呈谐音」

senses.title: Having similar vowel sounds
senses.definition: sharing similar vowel sounds, especially in nearby words or lines
senses.definitionCN: 共享相似元音，尤指邻近词语或诗行中
senses.example: The assonant chime of those syllables lingers.
senses.exampleCN: 那些音节谐和的鸣响久久萦绕。
senses.why: As the adjective of assonance, it describes what sounds toward what else.
senses.whyCN: 作为 assonance 的形容词，它描绘「朝彼此发声」的性质。

senses.title: Agreeing in sound generally
senses.definition: corresponding or agreeing in sound
senses.definitionCN: 在声音上相应或一致
senses.example: The two names are assonant enough to confuse listeners.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个名字音似到足以让听者混淆。
senses.why: Sounding toward becomes sounding alike in any context.
senses.whyCN: 「向对方发声」在任何语境中都引申为「听来相像」。

intro.en: Assonant comes from Latin assonans, the present participle of assonare, to sound toward.
intro.cn: assonant 源自拉丁语 assonans，即 assonare（向…发声）的现在分词。

items.en: The root *swen- meant to sound.
items.cn: 词根 *swen- 意为发声。

items.en: Sonare meant to make sound.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sonare 意为发声。

items.en: Assonans described something sounding in answer.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 assonans 形容应声之物。

items.en: Old French carried assonant into verse terminology.
items.cn: 古法语将 assonant 引入诗律术语。

items.en: English adopted assonant alongside assonance.
items.cn: 英语与 assonance 一同借入 assonant。

note.en: Assonant is the describing form of the echo that assonance names.
note.cn: assonant 是 assonance 所指回响的描述形式。

entries.definition: the noun for vowel-echo
entries.definitionCN: 元音韵（同根名词）

entries.definition: to show assonance
entries.definitionCN: 呈谐音（同根动词）

entries.definition: sounding together; also a speech sound
entries.definitionCN: 协和的；辅音（同根）

entries.definition: clashing in sound
entries.definitionCN: 刺耳的；不协和的（同根反前缀）

entries.definition: deep and echoing
entries.definitionCN: 洪亮回荡的（同根）

entries.definition: having corresponding ending sounds
entries.definitionCN: 押韵的

entries.definition: repeating initial consonants
entries.definitionCN: 押头韵的

entries.definition: pleasing to the ear
entries.definitionCN: 悦耳的

entries.definition: sweet-sounding
entries.definitionCN: 旋律优美的

entries.definition: alike in sound
entries.definitionCN: 同音的

normalIntro.en: Add -ant to assonance: something that is doing the vowel-echoing.
normalIntro.cn: 在 assonance 后加 -ant：表示「正在进行元音呼应的」。

normal.en: sonare means to sound, as in sonic.
normal.cn: sonare 意为发声，如 sonic。

normal.en: -ant marks the describing form.
normal.cn: -ant 标记形容词形式。

normal.en: opposite-sounding word is dissonant.
normal.cn: 声音相对的词是 dissonant。

normal.en: only vowels are compared in this word.
normal.cn: 这个词只比较元音。

normal.en: poets chain assonant vowels for music.
normal.cn: 诗人串联谐和元音制造乐感。

abstract.en: Picture twin lanterns glowing the same shade.
abstract.cn: 想象一对同色发光的双灯笼。

abstract.en: Hear two strings tuned to one pitch.
abstract.cn: 听两根琴弦调成同一音高。

abstract.en: Feel vowel letters as matching keys on a ring.
abstract.cn: 体会元音字母如同一串相配的钥匙。

examples.en: The assonant pattern repeats the long a sound.
examples.cn: 这一谐音模式重复长 a 音。

examples.en: Medieval chants often used assonant endings.
examples.cn: 中世纪圣咏常用元音韵结尾。

examples.en: Her assonant phrasing made the poem hum.
examples.cn: 她谐音的措辞让诗篇嗡嗡作响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额搜能特」——额搜出能特别应和的音，元音相似即 assonant。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ sonare（发声）→ assonans（应声的）→ 英语 assonant（谐音的）。

sensesIntro.en: The describing form of vowel-echo covers both poetic craft and plain likeness.

definition_en: molten rock stored beneath the surface of a planet, which may cool to form igneous rock or reach the surface as lava
core_image: 地表之下极深处，一汪橙红的黏稠熔体在岩壁间缓慢翻滚，被上方厚重的岩层死死压住
scene: 钻探船的甲板上，仪器显示地下深处有一层缓慢流动的高温熔体，压力正在上升。 Scientists drill into the ocean floor to sample the magma before it reaches the surface.
sceneCN: 这里 magma 指仍在地下的熔融岩石（第 1 个义项：位于地表之下、尚未喷出的熔融态岩石）；句意为科学家钻入海底，在岩浆到达地表之前取样。

senses.title: Molten rock underground
senses.definition: molten or partly molten rock stored beneath the surface of a planet
senses.definitionCN: 储存于行星地表之下、呈熔融或半熔融状态的岩石
senses.example: The magma rose slowly through a network of cracks.
senses.exampleCN: 岩浆沿着裂隙网络缓慢上升。
senses.why: Greek magma meant a kneaded mass; geologists applied it to rock softened by heat into a paste-like body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 magma 意为「揉成的团块」；地质学家用它指被热软化成糊状团块的岩石。

senses.title: A chamber that stores magma
senses.definition: a large body of magma held within the crust, often feeding a volcano
senses.definitionCN: 地壳中储存大量岩浆的腔体，常为火山提供补给
senses.example: Seismic surveys revealed a magma chamber three kilometres below the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 地震勘测显示峰顶下方三公里处有一个岩浆房。
senses.why: the mass had to be located somewhere, so the container sense grew out of the material sense.
senses.whyCN: 这团熔体总得存在于某处，于是「容器」义从「材料」义中生长出来。

senses.title: Magma typed by composition
senses.titleCN: 按成分划分的岩浆类型
senses.definition: a melt described by its chemical composition, such as basaltic or granitic magma
senses.definitionCN: 按化学成分描述的熔体，如玄武质岩浆或花岗质岩浆
senses.example: Basaltic magma is hotter and runnier than granitic melt.
senses.exampleCN: 玄武质岩浆比花岗质熔体更热、更稀。
senses.why: composition decides how a melt behaves, so the word came to name varieties rather than one substance.
senses.whyCN: 成分决定熔体的行为，因此这个词开始指称不同品种，而非单一物质。

senses.title: Any molten material
senses.definition: a general term for a hot melt, including molten metal, glass or ice
senses.definitionCN: 对高温熔体的泛称，包括熔融金属、玻璃或冰
senses.example: The furnace stirred a magma of molten glass and ash.
senses.exampleCN: 炉中翻搅着一团熔融玻璃与灰的混合物。
senses.why: the paste image is broad enough to cover industrial and planetary melts that are not rock.
senses.whyCN: 「糊状团块」的意象足够宽，可覆盖并非岩石的工业熔体与行星熔体。

senses.title: A planet-wide magma ocean
senses.definition: a global layer of molten rock on a young planet or moon
senses.definitionCN: 年轻行星或卫星上全球性的熔融岩石层
senses.example: The early Moon probably had a magma ocean hundreds of kilometres deep.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的月球可能有一层深达数百公里的岩浆洋。
senses.why: planetary science extended the underground body to the whole surface of a young world.
senses.whyCN: 行星科学把地下的熔体扩展到年轻天体的整个表面。

senses.title: Mixing of two magmas
senses.definition: the process in which two different magmas meet and blend, often before an eruption
senses.definitionCN: 两种不同岩浆相遇并混合的过程，常发生在喷发之前
senses.example: Textures in the lava record magma mixing just before the blast.
senses.exampleCN: 熔岩中的结构记录了爆发前一刻的岩浆混合。
senses.why: the word works as an attributive noun here, so the compound can name a process between two bodies of melt.
senses.whyCN: 在这个复合术语中该词作定语名词，因此整个复合词能指两团熔体之间的过程。

senses.title: The parent magma
senses.definition: the original melt from which a series of related rocks or melts are derived
senses.definitionCN: 一系列相关岩石或熔体所由衍生的原始熔体
senses.example: Geochemists traced all the samples back to one parental magma.
senses.exampleCN: 地球化学家把全部样品追溯至同一个母岩浆。
senses.why: the word works as a family term, with melts descending from a common source as children from a parent.
senses.whyCN: 该词被当作家族术语：各熔体如同子女，源自同一个母体。

senses.title: Suppressed fury like magma
senses.definition: a figurative use for strong feeling or power that is held down and may break out
senses.definitionCN: 比喻被压住、可能冲破而出的强烈情绪或力量
senses.example: Resentment had been gathering like magma beneath the quiet office.
senses.exampleCN: 怨气像岩浆一样在那间安静的办公室里积攒。
senses.why: magma is invisible and dangerous precisely because it is still under the crust, which makes it a natural image for held-in anger.
senses.whyCN: 岩浆之所以危险，正因为它仍在壳下、看不见，这使它成为压抑怒气的天然意象。

intro.en: Magma comes from Greek magma, a kneaded mass, from massein, to knead. Latin used magma only as a Greek loanword, so there is no native Latin family behind it. Geology adopted the term in the nineteenth century for molten rock still underground, specifically to contrast with lava at the surface.
intro.cn: magma 一般认为源自希腊 magma「揉成的团块」，出自动词 massein「揉、捏」，但更早的前希腊词根并不确定。拉丁语中的 magma 只是希腊借词，背后没有本土拉丁词族。地质学在十九世纪采用该词指仍在地下的熔融岩石，特意与已到地表的 lava 相对。

items.en: Massein meant to knead, press or work a soft substance with the hands.
items.cn: massein 意为「揉、压」，用手把柔软之物反复捏合。

items.en: Magma was the result: a kneaded mass, and in medical Greek a thick ointment or paste.
items.cn: magma 是结果：揉成的一团；在希腊医学中还指浓稠的药膏或糊剂。

items.en: Latin texts used magma as an unassimilated Greek word. It has no Latin verb or noun relatives, which is why this entry leaves the Latin list empty.
items.cn: 拉丁文献把 magma 当作未同化的希腊词使用。它没有拉丁动词或名词同族，因此本词条的拉丁词表留空。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology needed a word for melt that had not yet reached the surface; magma filled that gap.
items.cn: 十九世纪的地质学需要一个词指尚未到达地表的熔体，magma 正好补上这个空位。

items.en: The word now covers magma chambers, magma oceans, magma mixing and parental magma, and is also used figuratively.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖岩浆房、岩浆洋、岩浆混合与母岩浆，也被用于比喻。

items.en: Source uncertain (root in doubt): the Greek origin is generally accepted, from magma, a kneaded mass, and massein, to knead; but the deeper pre-Greek root of massein is unsettled, any older form offered for it is a reconstruction, and the exact date of the geological sense is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：一般认为是希腊 magma「揉成的团块」，出自 massein「揉、捏」，这一路径获较广泛接受；但 massein 更早的前希腊词根并无定论，凡给出的更深形式均属重构形式，地质义的确切首见年代亦为约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same word; group two holds the terms most often confused with magma.
note.cn: 第一组是由同一个词构成的形式；第二组是最容易与岩浆混淆的术语。

entries.definition: Relating to magma or to the processes that involve it, as in magmatic water or magmatic differentiation.
entries.definitionCN: 与岩浆或岩浆参与的过程有关，如岩浆水、岩浆分异。

entries.definition: The total activity of magma within a region, including its generation, movement and solidification.
entries.definitionCN: 一个区域内岩浆活动的总和，包括生成、运移与固结。

entries.definition: An uncommon plural modelled on Greek and Latin neuter plurals; magmas is the usual form.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿希腊语与拉丁语中性复数构成的少见复数；常用复数仍是 magmas。

entries.definition: The underground reservoir that holds magma; the phrase names the container, not the melt.
entries.definitionCN: 储存岩浆的地下储库；这个短语指容器，而非熔体本身。

entries.definition: The same molten rock once it has reached the surface; magma is the underground stage, lava the exposed stage.
entries.definitionCN: 同一种熔融岩石到达地表之后的名称；magma 是地下阶段，lava 是露出地表的阶段。

entries.definition: A plain description of rock heated until liquid; magma is the technical term for it underground.
entries.definitionCN: 对加热至液态的岩石的平实描述；magma 是它在地下时的术语。

entries.definition: In petrology, a synonym for liquid rock or the liquid portion of a partly molten system.
entries.definitionCN: 在岩石学中指液态岩石，或部分熔融体系中的液相部分。

entries.definition: Describing rock formed from cooled magma or lava; it names the product, not the molten stage.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由冷却的岩浆或熔岩形成的岩石；指产物，而非熔融阶段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphology, real collocations and the real magma-lava boundary.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊构词、真实搭配，以及真实存在的岩浆与熔岩分界。

normal.en: Greek massein means to knead: magma is rock softened and worked into a glowing paste.
normal.cn: 希腊 massein 意为「揉」：岩浆就是被揉软、揉成一团的灼热糊状岩石。

normal.en: Magma stays below, lava comes out: one word for the hidden stage, one for the exposed stage.
normal.cn: 岩浆留在地下，熔岩流到地表：一个词指隐藏阶段，一个词指露出阶段。

normal.en: Compound terms come in a series: magma chamber, magma ocean, magma mixing, parental magma.
normal.cn: 复合术语成串出现：岩浆房、岩浆洋、岩浆混合、母岩浆。

normal.en: Composition splits it into basaltic magma and granitic magma, the first hotter and runnier.
normal.cn: 按成分可分为玄武质岩浆与花岗质岩浆，前者更热、更稀。

normal.en: The figurative use keeps the position: anger sits under the surface like magma under crust.
normal.cn: 比喻用法保留了位置：怒气伏在表面之下，如同壳下的岩浆。

abstract.en: Picture dough being folded and pressed in a bowl until it becomes one soft mass.
abstract.cn: 想象面团在盆里被反复折叠按压，最后成了一团柔软的整体。

abstract.en: Picture a thick soup held down by a lid, steam bubbling only at the rim.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅浓汤被盖子压住，热气只在边缘冒出细泡。

abstract.en: Picture a hidden underground river that makes the ground above slightly warm.
abstract.cn: 想象地下有一条看不见的暗河，让上方的地面微微发烫。

examples.en: The magma cooled slowly at depth, forming coarse crystals.
examples.cn: 岩浆在深处缓慢冷却，形成粗大的晶体。

examples.en: A magma chamber beneath the caldera was detected by seismic waves.
examples.cn: 地震波探测到破火山口下方有一个岩浆房。

examples.en: Her anger sat like magma, unseen until the day it broke through.
examples.cn: 她的怒气像岩浆一样伏着，直到爆发那天才被看见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 希腊语「揉成的团」——地热把岩石揉软，还压在地壳里 → 岩浆

root: 希腊 magma「揉成的团块」，出自 massein「揉、捏」；拉丁语仅作希腊借词使用，无本土同族；地质学借指地下熔融岩石，与地表的 lava（熔岩）分工。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hidden body: a kneaded melt that sits under rock. The material sense comes first, then its container, its composition, the wider class of melts, planetary and process uses, a source term, and finally the figurative pressure it suggests.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个隐藏的物体：一团伏在岩石之下的熔体。先讲物质本身，再讲容器、成分、更宽的熔体类别、行星与过程用法、源熔体，最后落在它暗示的压抑之势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kneaded, glowing paste trapped under a lid of rock.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团被岩石盖子压住的灼热糊状物。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND CONTAINER: the melt itself, and the cavity that holds it.
branches.cn: 物质与容器：熔体本身，以及容纳它的腔体。

branches.en: COMPOSITION AND SOURCE: chemistry sorts the melt into types, and one type can be the parent of a rock series.
branches.cn: 成分与来源：化学把熔体分成类型，而某一类型可以成为一套岩石系列的母体。

branches.en: BEYOND ROCK: the same paste image covers industrial melts and a planet-wide molten layer.
branches.cn: 越出岩石：同一个糊状意象覆盖工业熔体与全球性的熔融层。

branches.en: PROCESS BETWEEN BODIES: two melts can meet and blend before an eruption.
branches.cn: 两团之间的过程：两股熔体可以在喷发前相遇并混合。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE PRESSURE: what is held under the crust becomes the image of held-in fury.
branches.cn: 比喻压力：压在壳下之物，成为被压抑怒气的意象。

intro.en: Magma is not built from Latin prefixes and suffixes; it is a whole Greek noun borrowed intact, so these items are stems and compounds rather than derivational endings.
intro.cn: magma 不是由拉丁前缀与后缀构成的，而是整体借入的希腊名词；因此下列条目是词干与复合形式，而非派生词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes no native relatives: magma appears only as a Greek loanword, and the geological vocabulary is built by compounding with English and Latin elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有提供本土同族词：magma 只作为希腊借词出现，地质词汇靠英语与拉丁成分复合构成。

items.example: The stem magma- appears unchanged in English.
items.exampleCN: 词干 magma- 在英语中保持原形。

items.example: Magmatic describes anything that belongs to magma.
items.exampleCN: magmatic 描述一切属于岩浆的事物。

items.structure: -ismos (Greek noun suffix of activity or system)
items.example: Magmatism names the activity of magma in a region.
items.exampleCN: magmatism 指一个区域内的岩浆活动。

items.example: Magmatology is the study of magmas and their evolution.
items.exampleCN: 岩浆学是研究岩浆及其演化的学问。

items.example: The chamber fed the eruption for several weeks.
items.exampleCN: 这个岩浆房为喷发供给了数周。

items.example: The magma ocean solidified from the top down.
Magma mixing can trigger an eruption.
items.exampleCN: 岩浆混合可能触发喷发。

items.meaning: source melt of a rock series
items.meaningCN: 一套岩石系列的源熔体
items.example: The parental magma was rich in magnesium.

items.meaning: change of melt composition by crystal separation
items.meaningCN: 熔体成分因晶体分离而改变
items.example: Magmatic differentiation produces different rock types.
items.exampleCN: 岩浆分异产生不同的岩石类型。

items.example: Basaltic magma feeds quiet lava flows.
items.exampleCN: 玄武质岩浆供给平静的熔岩流。
